    #6930. Breaking: Why The World's Largest Commercial Jet Engine Is A Threat To Other Powerplants

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1589 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Why The World's Largest Commercial Jet Engine Is A Threat To Other Powerplants

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1589 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that brandon's passion for aviation started at a young age.
    • It has been revealed that GE Aerospace describes the GE9X as the largest and most powerful commercial aircraft engine ever built, and the specifications support the claim.
    • Recent findings suggest that where the engine matters commercially is on an aircraft it has never powered.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that brandon's passion for aviation started at a young age. He became involved in the flight simulator and VATSIM communities, which sparked his interest in aviation and eventually led him to earn his private pilot license. Outside of work, he continues to build flight hours, explore fresh airports, and stay involved in the aviation community.

    It has been revealed that GE Aerospace describes the GE9X as the largest and most powerful commercial aircraft engine ever built, and the specifications support the claim. A 134-inch front fan, a composite fan case, ceramic matrix composites in the hot section, and a 60:1 overall pressure ratio make it the most advanced large turbofan in production, and Guinness World Records certifies it as the most powerful commercial jet engine by test performance. None of that puts competitive pressure on anyone, because the engine has no rival to fight. GE holds the 777X exclusively, as it has held every 777 variant since the 777-200LR.

    Recent findings suggest that where the engine matters commercially is on an aircraft it has never powered. Rolls-Royce has supplied the only engine ever offered on the Airbus A350, a position no competitor has challenged in two decades, and Airbus is now studying a stretched version of that aircraft aimed at the roughly 400-seat market the 777-9 currently has to itself. A stretch of that size needs more thrust than the Trent XWB-97 produces, and the GE9X sits in exactly that class. Airbus has looked at the idea. By most accounts, GE has not shown much appetite for it.

    The headline dimension is the front fan, which measures 134 inches across and carries 16 fourth-generation carbon fiber composite blades inside a composite fan case. GE’s product material claims that this makes the fan larger than a Boeing 737 fuselage. Key.Aero frames the comparison more precisely, describing the engine’s overall diameter, rather than the fan alone, as greater than the fuselage diameter of the 737 family. Either way, the GE9X is the largest installation ever hung under a commercial wing.

    Industry observers note that thrust needs the same care. Guinness World Records lists the GE9X at a maximum thrust of 134,300 pounds, achieved during an engineering test at GE’s outdoor facility in Peebles, Ohio, on November 10, 2017, breaking the 127,900 pounds the GE90-115B recorded in 2002. Guinness also lists the engine’s rated thrust as 110,000 pounds and notes that the record reflects testing conditions rather than commercial operation. For service on the 777-9, the engine is certified to 105,000 pounds. The record figure therefore describes what the architecture can produce at its limits, not what a flight crew will ever command.

    Efficiency is where the design earns its reputation. GE puts the GE9X at approximately a 10:1 bypass ratio and a 60:1 overall pressure ratio, with specific fuel consumption up to 10% better than the GE90-115B. Ceramic matrix composites appear in the combustor liner and the high-pressure turbine shrouds, parts that tolerate higher temperatures with less cooling air than the metal components they replace. GE says the engine received FAA certification in September 2020, after 27,000 cycles and 17,000 hours of testing.

    According to recent reports, every A350 ever built flies behind the same engine. Rolls-Royce supplies the Trent XWB as the family’s sole powerplant across a thrust range. Simple Flying puts it at 84,000 to 97,000 pounds, and no alternative has ever been offered to a customer. For a widebody that has sold in A350 numbers, that is unusual, and it exists because of a decision GE made rather than a competition Rolls-Royce won.

    Sources indicate that aero-News Network reported in 2008 that GE executives had told Airbus the tech giant would not build an engine to compete with the GE90 it supplies for the 777, leaving Airbus with a Trent variant as its only option for the A350. Airbus sales chief John Leahy had already closed the other door, saying, “We have no intention of putting their GEnx engine on the A350 at all.” GE’s view was that the GEnx suited the smaller A350 variants but could not economically scale to the thrust the A350-1000 required.

    Recent findings suggest that commercially, the refusal was straightforward. GE is the exclusive engine supplier for the 777-200LR, the 777-300ER and the 777 freighter, and the A350-1000 was designed to take sales from precisely those aircraft. Developing a 97,000-pound engine for Airbus would have handed airlines a GE-powered alternative to a GE-powered Boeing, buying a share of one program at the cost of a monopoly on another. Rolls-Royce, which had lost the 777 engine competition to the GE90, took the work instead and has held the position ever since.

    Airbus has been circling a larger A350 for most of 2026. Commercial aircraft CEO Lars Wagner told the media in Toulouse that a decision on stretching both the A350 and the A220 would come before 2030, adding that there is “clearly” demand from the industry for longer versions of each. Aerospace Global News reported that Wagner tied both projects to viable business cases and board approval, while acknowledging that customers are waiting for each aircraft.

    Thrust is the obstacle that makes the engine question unavoidable. AIN reported that a stretch would need more thrust than the A350-1000’s Trent XWB-97 can provide, and that the alternatives are limited. By AIN’s reckoning, one option would be the GE9X that powers the 777-9, an engine already certified in the class a 400-seat Airbus would require. Rolls-Royce has signaled nothing publicly about an XWB above 97,000 pounds, leaving the stretch dependent either on an unannounced derivative or on a supplier Airbus has never used on the program.

    In a recent development, wagner’s own answer was carefully incomplete. Pressed by reporters on whether Rolls-Royce would automatically keep its exclusive position on a prospective A350-2000, he declined to confirm it, and he declined to specify whether Airbus is engaged with GE Aerospace on supplying engines for the aircraft. He did say Airbus is happy with Rolls-Royce and that the exclusive partnership “works well” for the A350 family. Those two positions aren't contradictory, but together they fall short of the commitment Rolls-Royce has enjoyed since the program began.

    In a recent development, the obstacle to the GE9X on an A350 is not Rolls-Royce. Reuters reported in October that industry sources say Airbus has toyed with using a GE Aerospace engine for the roughly 400-seat A350-2000, but that the engine maker has so far shown limited interest in joining. Airbus, in other words, has considered the option and GE has not pursued it.

    According to recent reports, nothing about the underlying arithmetic has changed since 2008. GE holds the 777X exclusively, and a 400-seat A350 would compete directly against the 777-9 rather than against the aging 777-300ER. Supplying an engine for that aircraft would mean competing with a program GE already owns outright, at a moment when the 777X backlog represents years of engine deliveries and decades of aftermarket revenue. AIN noted the politics of an Airbus-GE widebody partnership as a complication in its own right, separate from the engineering.

    According to recent reports, practical constraints sit on top of the commercial ones. The GE9X has no application outside the 777X, which means every development dollar spent adapting it for an Airbus wing would serve a single prospective customer on an aircraft that has not been released. GE is also still closing out problems with the engine it has. AIN listed a variable guide-vane matter and, more recently, a mid-seal durability issue among the technical challenges the engine has encountered during 777-9 flight testing. An engine maker working through durability findings on its newest product is not an obvious candidate to open a second airframe program.

    Recent findings suggest that volume is the real measure of the GE9X’s position. At the Dubai Airshow on November 17, 2025, Emirates ordered 65 additional 777-9s worth $38 billion at list prices, taking its total Boeing orderbook to 315 widebodies; 270 777Xs, 10 777 freighters and 35 787s. The same announcement raised the airline’s GE9X commitment to 540 engines, including 130 added that day, making Emirates the largest GE9X customer by a wide margin. Deliveries from that orderbook run through 2038.

    Emirates also bought optionality that could extend the engine’s run. The carrier signed up for options to convert its latest 777-9 order into the 777-10 or the 777-8, which Emirates described as backing for Boeing’s feasibility study on the larger 777-10. Any 777-10 would use the same engine, since no alternative exists for the airframe.

    Certification is what stands between the backlog and revenue. GE identified a durability problem with the GE9X mid-seal after a crack was found during a January 2026 shop visit on a 777X flight-test engine, a component chief financial officer Rahul Ghai described as “one of the parts that connects the front and the back of the engine.” Air Data News reported that the FAA will not certify the 777-9 until it approves the redesigned seal, citing an agency official speaking to FlightGlobal; GE is seeking that approval by the end of 2026, and Boeing is still targeting first delivery in 2027. Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg said in September that “We may see some of the testing spill into next year,” because GE had needed more testing than expected to validate the fix. Reuters has put the program six years behind schedule, with more than $15 billion in charges.

    Aer Lingus Retrofitting A330s With Newly introduced Business, Premium Economy, Economy Cabins

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (656 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It’s not just Aer Lingus’ premium economy stealing the headlines in Ireland today.
    • Sources indicate that the same 10 Airbus A330s that will get the airline’s newly introduced premium economy will also get a swanky new business class.
    • Aer Lingus opted for its take on the ever-popular Collins Elevation suite.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It’s not just Aer Lingus’ premium economy stealing the headlines in Ireland today. Expected to fly passengers for the first time on October 1, 2027, the fresh cabins are part of a comprehensive Airbus A330 tip-to-tail retrofit that will include new business and economy cabins. We covered the premium economy cabin in a separate article story.

    Sources indicate that the same 10 Airbus A330s that will get the airline’s newly introduced premium economy will also get a swanky new business class. The airline’s Airbus A321XLRs aren’t included in this cabin update.

    Aer Lingus opted for its take on the ever-popular Collins Elevation suite. There’ll be 28 seats in a 1-2-1 configuration that stretch out to 78 inches long when in lie-flat mode.

    The color palette of Irish greens, whites, and light wood gives the seat an elegant yet distinctly non-corporate feel. It’s a thumbs-up from me.

    In terms of updated tech, each seat has 4K HD screens (in all cabins) as well as wireless and USB-C charging. While nothing revolutionary, these touches will significantly modernize Aer Lingus A330 cabins.

    Aer Lingus is also introducing a self-service bar stocked with snacks and drinks. I wonder if this will include Champagne….

    The airline will also serve up a whole fresh in-flight dining experience featuring dishes inspired by both Irish ingredients and its transatlantic destinations.

    It wouldn’t be a full retrofit without sprucing up economy.

    In a recent development, per the renderings, Aer Lingus has done a great job again with the cabin’s look and feel. The emerald green Shamrocks are a lovely touch.

    Seats are configured in the A330’s classic 2-4-2 configuration — a favorite for those traveling in pairs.

    While the recline looks a bit modest here, the seat’s thickness looks like it’ll provide more support than some of those ultra-thin, rigid seats airlines are sneaking in these days.

    The six-way adjustable headrests should also mean less head-wobbling when catching some shut-eye.

    The curved design of the seat backs should hopefully mean noticeably more knee space.

    Recent findings suggest that aer Lingus is also upping its food and beverage ante for economy passengers. In addition to a snack bar, a new mid-flight snack will be offered.

    A retrofit program like this was essential for Aer Lingus to remain competitive in the transatlantic market. The introduction of premium economy was a great move, especially since the cabin is known to be highly profitable.

    Aer Lingus has also done a great job of matching the Irish color scheme and sleek design across all cabins, which is more than can be said for some airlines these days. 😉.

    What do you make of Aer Lingus’ fresh A330 cabins?

    Beginner’s luck: Freshmen leave it to chance at House office lottery

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (903 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Rep.-elect Mark Teixeira reacts after drawing the worst chip during Tuesday’s lottery for newly elected members of Congress.
    • As far as birthdays go, Rep.-elect Shannon Taylor was having a pretty good one.
    • Crowded into a room in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday morning with the rest of her freshman class, the Virginia Democrat walked up to a table with a wooden box and reached in.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rep.-elect Mark Teixeira reacts after drawing the worst chip during Tuesday’s lottery for newly elected members of Congress. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    As far as birthdays go, Rep.-elect Shannon Taylor was having a pretty good one.

    Crowded into a room in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday morning with the rest of her freshman class, the Virginia Democrat walked up to a table with a wooden box and reached in.

    “This is so nervewracking,” she mentioned, before pulling out a chip with a “1” printed on it.

    According to recent reports, her prize was a coveted one — first choice of office space. Every two years, incoming members of the House play a game of chance to see who can land the best real estate and who will be relegated to less desirable corners of the Capitol complex.

    The room broke out in raucous applause and a standing ovation. Her new colleagues started singing “Happy Birthday.”.

    It has been revealed that not everyone was so lucky. Rep.-elect Mark Teixeira, R-Texas, pulled number 105 — the very last one. The former MLB player raised his arms in a mock celebration.

    “Lets all hope for the luck of the Taylors,” said Rep.-elect Brent Taylor, R-Tenn., only to emerge with number 81.

    The newly-elected members got their turn in a random order, walking up one by one to a table where deputy executive director of House Office Buildings Kornell Rancy kept watch over the box of chips.

    Rep.-elect John Cowan, R-Ga., was the first to pick a number. The first neurosurgeon to be elected to Congress, Cowan wore his white doctor’s coat as he pulled number 11 out of the box.

    “I wanted to do something where I’m just representing health care providers around the country,” Cowan stated.

    As returning members lay claim to more desirable offices made available by those who resign, retire or lose elections, the space they’ve abandoned is left for the newcomers, who are on the Hill this week for orientation. Many of them will end up in the Longworth Building, where suites can be awkward or cramped.

    Sources indicate that not all offices are created equal, and the calculus has changed over the years. The previously undesirable Cannon Building just underwent a budget-busting renovation that lasted more than a decade, with a spacious courtyard opening earlier this year. But the coveted Rayburn Building still retains its prestige, despite repeated and dire warnings from the Architect of the Capitol about its crumbling infrastructure.

    “You’re welcome,” mentioned Rep.-elect Amish Shah, D-Ariz., after pulling a disappointing number 94.

    Prior to the lottery, Rep.-elect Trever Nehls, R-Texas, was hoping for the best but had a backup plan in case his number said otherwise.

    “If I don’t pick number one, I’m going to offer one of these cigars as a trade to whoever gets it,” he noted, pointing to three of them sticking out of his jacket pocket. He’s preparing to take over the seat presently held by his twin brother Troy, who shares a fondness for stogies.

    It has been revealed that the office space lottery dates back to 1908, when members of the 60th Congress received their first office assignments after the completion of what would be named the Cannon Building. A House page drew names and numbers from a box, and members selected their offices from a chart, according to House Office Buildings executive director of facility operations Joe Yates, who kicked things off Tuesday with a history lesson.

    The lottery now is a little more modern, with members poring over virtual office layouts and doing walkthroughs of spaces on laptops.

    “If somebody had to get 105, I’m glad it was me because I am here to serve, and I’m serving my freshman class by picking the worst office,” Teixeira said. “This is low on my priority list.”.

    Some members announced their lucky draws themselves, while others let Yates break the news.

    “Come visit me,” noted Rep.-elect Chris Gober, R-Texas, after pulling number 2 from the box.

    After the lottery itself, members huddled with their staff to strategize about the next steps — how to leverage their numbers and select the best suites left on the list, while also exploring layouts, paint colors and carpeting.

    In a recent development, “First and foremost, a good layout, so we can do good work, and people can be comfortable in doing the work, and then a convenient location. Very utilitarian,” said Rep.-elect Scott Wiener, D-Calif., of his priorities.

    “We’ll get a decent Longworth office,” said Wiener, who drew pick 43. “Cannon would have been ideal, but I’m happy with any office.”.

    Rep.-elect Manny Rutinel, D-Colo., was hoping to replicate the good luck of some of his colleagues. “I’m going to do the Shannon Taylor and Sam Forstag. It’s eyes closed, behind the back,” he noted of his moves, reaching into the box. But it wasn’t enough, and Rutinel pulled number 69.

    “These are not red numbers, these are not blue numbers. These are the remaining numbers, and there ain’t that many,” stated Rep.-elect Johnny Garcia, D-Texas, who was among the last few people to pick. He emerged with number 75.

    And when Rep.-elect Joe Strada, R-Fla., the last of the incoming members to draw, walked up to the table, the whole room cheered.

    “Wouldn’t it be crazy if I picked number 1?” he joked, pulling out the last chip in the box.

    Southwest Signs Interline Deal With French Bee

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (314 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Airlinegeeks

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that southwest and French Bee are joining forces to expand international travel options for passengers not only on both sides of the Atlantic, but also the Pacific.
    • The agreement connects French Bee’s international network with Southwest’s extensive domestic network in the U.S.
    • French Bee also flies to Newark, New Jersey, but Southwest does not offer service there.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that southwest and French Bee are joining forces to expand international travel options for passengers not only on both sides of the Atlantic, but also the Pacific. The two carriers announced a new interline partnership that will allow travelers to combine flights on both airlines under a single ticket.

    The agreement connects French Bee’s international network with Southwest’s extensive domestic network in the U.S. The partnership will provide connections through French Bee’s three U.S. gateway airports that Southwest also serves: Los Angeles, Miami, and San Francisco.

    French Bee also flies to Newark, New Jersey, but Southwest does not offer service there.

    Passengers will be able to connect between French Bee’s international flights and Southwest domestic flights without having to purchase separate tickets for each airline or recheck bags at each airline.

    French Bee operates an all-Airbus A350 fleet, with its primary hub located at Paris-Orly Airport, and operations to North America and destinations in the Indian Ocean and South Pacific.

    Southwest passengers will gain access to French Bee destinations not only from Paris, but also Tahiti in French Polynesia, which the French carrier flies to from San Francisco. The partnership will also offer one-stop French Bee connections from Paris to the Maldives and Sri Lanka, scheduled to launch in December 2026, along with current flights to Reunion Island.

    For French Bee customers, the latest arrangement provides access to a much larger network of domestic destinations throughout the U.S. Southwest’s network includes cities such as Las Vegas, Chicago, Dallas, Denver, Nashville, Austin, San Diego, Phoenix, and multiple destinations in the Hawaiian Islands.

    The agreement represents another step in Southwest’s expanding international connectivity strategy, as the airline continues to develop relationships with overseas carriers rather than rely exclusively on its own international operations with its all-Boeing 737 fleet.

    Tickets for connecting flights are now available through French Bee’s website.

    In a recent development, world of Hyatt members can expect more flexibility and choice from January 1, 2027. Highlights of the upgrade include earning Milestone Rewards sooner, a bunch of upcoming Milestone Rewards, and more flexibility when redeeming rewards and paying for stays. There’s actually no huge catch, and the changes I learned about last night on an intimate call with the Hyatt team are genuinely member-focused.

    The update follows the new Hyatt-Delta relationship, which also released this week.

    It has been revealed that starting January 1, 2027, World of Hyatt members will start enjoying Milestone Rewards after 10 nights stayed or 20,000 base points. That’s great news for relatively infrequent Hyatt guests (like myself), who will no longer have to stay 20 nights or earn 35,000 base points to earn their first Milestone Reward.

    At 10 nights or 20,000 base points, members will be able to choose from:.

    Milestone Rewards will be unlocked at every ten nights, up to 150 nights.

    It has been revealed that not only is it about to become quicker to earn Milestone Rewards, but there’ll also be new awards to choose from each level. Here are a few examples of the 20+ new rewards:.

    Sources indicate that the downside of free parking becoming a Milestone Reward means that World of Hyatt members who earn Globalist from 2027 onwards will no longer enjoy it as a permanent status perk on award stays. This will be a notable downgrade to Globalists who value their parking perk.

    Hyatt has published a handy new infographic with all the details.

    There are also two more crucial Milestone Reward changes to note, both of which aren’t such positive news:.

    For the first time, World of Hyatt members will be able to stack multiple awards on a single stay. For example, you can use a Suite Upgrade Voucher, a Guest of Honor Award, and claim free parking, all on the same stay.

    All awards will also expire after 365 of being issued. That’s great for awards that used to only last 180 days.

    Sources indicate that I think this could be my favorite upgrade. Hyatt is enhancing its Pay My Way option to allow guests to choose how to pay for each night of a stay.     The booking page will display each award applied to each individual night and provide guests with a drop-down menu to select how they’d like to pay for each night.

Even when you consider some of the less favorable updates, like Globalists losing free parking and some award expiration dates being limited to 365 days, the changes will be positive overall for the vast majority of World of Hyatt members.

    #6923. Industry News: Too Fast? United Airlines' Starlink Rollout Is So Rapid, Some Planes Still Have Their Old WiFi Antennas

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1325 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Too Fast? United Airlines' Starlink Rollout Is So Rapid, Some Planes Still Have Their Old WiFi Antennas

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1325 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • United Airlines has been steadily improving its product and customer experience to move upmarket and compete head-on with Delta Air Lines, the premium leader in the US, for years.
    • Sources indicate that but in 2024, United revealed that it would install Starlink WiFi across its entire mainline and regional fleets, comprising over 1,600 aircraft.
    • It has been revealed that starlink, a subsidiary of SpaceX, is a relatively newly introduced player in the inflight WiFi market.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    United Airlines has been steadily improving its product and customer experience to move upmarket and compete head-on with Delta Air Lines, the premium leader in the US, for years. The carrier has made genuine shifts and has been rewarded with improving financials, to the point that it now regularly posts results nearly as impressive as Delta's. One weak point, however, is that the airline's onboard WiFi systems have lagged behind what competitors offered going into the 2020s.

    Sources indicate that but in 2024, United revealed that it would install Starlink WiFi across its entire mainline and regional fleets, comprising over 1,600 aircraft. It aims to complete Starlink retrofits by the end of 2027, which is an ambitious target given the sheer size of the combined fleet. To achieve this promptly, the airline is rapidly sending aircraft for retrofits, and United has placed such an emphasis on speed that it's installing Starlink on some aircraft without removing their legacy systems.

    It has been revealed that starlink, a subsidiary of SpaceX, is a relatively newly introduced player in the inflight WiFi market. However, Starlink systems provide much faster onboard connectivity than those offered by companies such as Viasat, Thales, or Panasonic, and the tech giant even formerly mandated that airline customers offer it to passengers for free (this is reportedly no longer the case). As such, it's become extremely popular with passengers, while airlines have been lining up for the service.

    United announced Starlink in September 2024, with the roll-out beginning in 2025. It later announced that it aimed to have all mainline and regional aircraft equipped with Starlink by the end of 2027, which meant an extremely rapid roll-out given the sheer size of the fleet. Initially, United focused on retrofitting Starlink onto the United Express fleet, as the service contract for the providers on this fleet was set to end shortly. Soon afterward, Starlink started coming to mainline.

    The official United Starlink tracker indicates that all Bombardier CRJ550s and Embraer E175s have been completed. 346 narrowbody aircraft have been retrofitted, and United has installed Starlink on the Airbus A321neo, A321XLR, Boeing 737-800, 737-900ER, 737 MAX 8, and 737 MAX 9. In addition, United has now installed Starlink on four 777-200ERs, one 777-300ER, and two 787-8s. Overall, about 46% of the fleet is retrofitted: 705 aircraft out of the 1,632 aircraft flying for United and United Express.

    In a recent development, earlier this month, a United 737-900ER was spotted parked at a gate and shared on X with two Starlink antennas (United's standard configuration for the system) and its older Viasat antenna. Similarly, a 737-900 was also spotted, equipped with Starlink and Viasat antennas, according to an X post.

    In a recent development, one advertised benefit of Starlink is quick installation, but it appears the main holdup in the retrofit project is the time required to remove the aircraft's previous WiFi equipment. On some aircraft, the airline simply left it on for now to speed up the process.

    It has been revealed that united has just over a year remaining until its end-of-2027 deadline, and only 46% of the fleet is completed. There's a high chance that this timeline could slip, but Starlink is meant to be a major commercial advantage for the airline. A clean Starlink installation is advertised as taking as little as eight hours, which is significantly faster than installation times for other WiFi systems. However, the full retrofit also requires removing the previous WiFi system, which can add significantly more time.

    According to recent reports, united states that its full timeline, including removing the legacy system, is about three to four days. To get the entire fleet retrofitted by the end of 2027, it would need to have a significant number of aircraft out of service, which is lost revenue. Therefore, the carrier has decided to shorten the timeline for N78438 and N37409 by leaving the Viasat system on for the time being, and it remains to be seen whether it will continue this practice in the future.

    Industry observers note that starlink is now flying on United's Bombardier and Embraer aircraft, along with the A321neo, 737, 777, and 787. However, it still operates a substantial number of aircraft with older WiFi systems. All the non-Starlink widebodies are equipped with Panasonic systems, while the narrowbody fleet features a mix of Panasonic, Viasat, and Thales systems. While Starlink is offered for free, the other systems generally require payment upfront, and none of the three offers the same speeds as Starlink.

    American Airlines generally offers Viasat WiFi on its domestic fleet, which is complimentary for AAdvantage members, while most of the widebodies are equipped with Panasonic systems. Delta offers either Viasat or Hughes WiFi on nearly its entire fleet. The benefit is that Viasat and Hughes offer much faster speeds than Panasonic and Thales. The downside for these airlines is that Starlink offers even faster speeds. But for United, it's now offering the fastest and slowest WiFi systems among its rivals.

    United is banking on Starlink becoming a major commercial advantage over its rivals, but it will only be a true advantage once the system is available across United's entire fleet. A better WiFi system on its own is not necessarily a reason for customers to choose one airline over the other, but it's becoming an increasingly vital factor in purchasing decisions. As United continues to aim for product and a premium brand, Starlink is becoming increasingly important to the airline's selling proposition.

    In a recent development, by moving upmarket and becoming a 'premium' airline brand, United is hoping to be a carrier that wins customers' business based on its name and product. This is the strategy that Delta first implemented under CEO Richard Anderson after its 2008 merger with Northwest Airlines, and Delta is now the most successful airline in the country. But of course, the US carriers don't make their money by selling flight tickets; rather, the money is in loyalty programs.

    Sources indicate that united has been tremendously successful in pursuing this strategy, and Starlink is meant to be a crucial advantage. United CEO Scott Kirby has publicly mentioned Starlink is a major selling point for the airline and that the carrier waited until competitors committed to systems like those offered by Viasat to gain an edge. Of course, while Starlink is a major competitive advantage for United, this won't necessarily be true across the US.

    American Airlines announced in May that it would install Starlink across its entire Airbus fleet, consisting of the A319-100, A320-200, A321-200, and A321neo, to begin in 2027. Last month, however, the carrier announced that it would expand the Starlink program to all mainline aircraft. The carrier has not stated that Starlink will come to the American Eagle fleet, but it will significantly elevate American's overall product offering as it also tries to move upmarket and become a premium brand.

    Recent findings suggest that delta, on the other hand, has not signed a deal with Starlink at all. Instead, Delta has committed to installing Amazon's upcoming Leo system on approximately half of its fleet. Reportedly, Delta and Starlink experienced conflicts about integrating the system into Delta's existing 'Delta Sync' portal, while there may have also been a personal conflict with Starlink CEO Elon Musk. However, the actual decision to go with Amazon would undoubtedly have been made after considering multiple factors as part of a larger commercial deal.

    Industry observers note that the issue for Delta is that Amazon Leo is not in service yet. The airline plans to begin installing Leo in 2028, when United is supposed to have already completed its Starlink retrofit. While the Viasat and Hughes systems Delta already offers are competent and free, Starlink offers faster speeds, and United has now established itself as the leader in the US airline industry, whereas Delta used to be. Considering how brand-conscious Delta is, this is not an enviable position.

    Rep. James Comer introduces 2027 bid for Kentucky governor

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, kentucky Rep.
    • Comer, whose role as chairman of the House Oversight Committee gave him a powerful platform to investigate Democrats, including former Presidents Joe Biden and Bill Clinton, has debuted a run for governor next year.
    • In a recent development, the Republican, who was just elected to a sixth full term representing Kentucky’s 1st District, is seeking to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, kentucky Rep. James Comer, here talking to reporters on Capitol Hill in June, is running for governor. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Kentucky Rep. James R. Comer, whose role as chairman of the House Oversight Committee gave him a powerful platform to investigate Democrats, including former Presidents Joe Biden and Bill Clinton, has debuted a run for governor next year.

    In a recent development, the Republican, who was just elected to a sixth full term representing Kentucky’s 1st District, is seeking to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear. Kentucky is one of three states holding off-year gubernatorial elections in 2027, alongside Louisiana and Mississippi.

    In his announcement at a tele-town hall Monday night, Comey emphasized pocketbook issues, pledging to eliminate the state income tax and boost job-creation in Louisville.

    “If we get that income tax to zero, people are going to have more money to spend, and we're going to be able to attract more good-paying jobs to Kentucky, which will be able to keep our best and brightest in the state,’’ he stated.

    According to recent reports, as the leader of the House Oversight panel, Comer has been at the forefront in the fight over the release of records related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. (Last week, the committee released a report concluding that the federal government mishandled criminal probes into Epstein’s activities.).

    Comer is a staunch ally of President Donald Trump, who carried Kentucky by 31 points in 2024, and his hard-nosed style of politics is conveyed in a soft-spoken Southern drawl.

    According to recent reports, known back home as Jamie, Comer has deep roots in rural Monroe County, dating back to the late 1700s. Prior to coming to Congress, he operated a farm before serving 11 years in the Kentucky House. In 2011, he was elected as the commonwealth’s commissioner of agriculture.

    Recent findings suggest that he made an unsuccessful run for governor in 2015, losing the Republican primary by 83 votes to Matt Bevin, who went on to win the general election. The following year, Comer easily won election to the House from his western Kentucky district, succeeding Republican Ed Whitfield.

    Recent findings suggest that comer has moved promptly to consolidate GOP support for his gubernatorial bid. He already has the backing of Kentucky Sen. Rand Paul and Sen.-elect Andy Barr. Michael Adams, Kentucky’s term-limited secretary of state who’d been seen a potential contender, gave Comer an early endorsement this summer.

    Industry observers note that while Comer enters the race as the Republican front-runner, he won’t have the field to himself. Other declared hopefuls include local prosecutor Rick Hardin and distiller Charles “Bruiser” Martin, who appeared on the Discovery Channel show “Moonshiners: Master Distiller.”.

    While Kentucky has in recent decades grown reliably Republican at the federal level, the GOP has won just two gubernatorial elections there over the past half century. Two high-profile Democrats have already launched bids to keep the governor’s mansion in party hands: Lt. Gov. Jacqueline Coleman and former state House Majority Leader and Beshear adviser Rocky Adkins, who ran for governor in 2019.

    In a statement Tuesday, the Democratic Governors Association dismissed Comer as “a job-killing, pro-war politician who looks down on everyday Kentuckians.”.

    #6920. Lufthansa’s A380 Business Class Seat Retrofit Nearly Done, But It Isn’t Allegris

    Lufthansa’s A380 Business Class Seat Retrofit Nearly Done, But It Isn’t Allegris

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1239 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In January 2026, Lufthansa formally announced aims to retrofit its Airbus A380s with new business class seats.
    • There’s now a positive upgrade, as it looks like Lufthansa is running way ahead on that schedule, and all A380s should be retrofitted within the coming weeks….
    • Sources indicate that lufthansa is introducing a new business class product on its entire fleet of eight Airbus A380s.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In January 2026, Lufthansa formally announced aims to retrofit its Airbus A380s with new business class seats. The first plane with new cabins entered service in April 2026, and Lufthansa had committed to retrofitting all the planes by the middle of 2027.

    There’s now a positive upgrade, as it looks like Lufthansa is running way ahead on that schedule, and all A380s should be retrofitted within the coming weeks….

    Sources indicate that lufthansa is introducing a new business class product on its entire fleet of eight Airbus A380s. Rather interestingly, it’s only business class that’s getting new seats, while first class, premium economy, and economy, remain the same, aside from some minor upgrades (like improved inflight entertainment).

    Sources indicate that the first A380 with new interiors entered service in April 2026, and AeroRoutes flags how as of December 18, 2026, Lufthansa is exclusively showing the new business class configuration on all routes. So starting in the coming weeks, you can expect the entire A380 network to feature the new cabins.

    Lufthansa A380s are based in Munich (MUC), and currently fly to Bangkok (BKK), Delhi (DEL), Los Angeles (LAX), Mumbai (BOM), San Francisco (SFO), and Washington (IAD). As you’d expect, there’s seasonal variation in the routes, though.

    What’s interesting is that Lufthansa isn’t introducing its fresh Allegris business class on these planes, but instead, is introducing another “off the shelf” product. Specifically, the airline has opted for the Thompson Aero Vantage XL product, which is in a staggered configuration.

    It has been revealed that each seat has direct aisle access, seat width of 58cm, and a bed length of at least two meters. Seats feature bluetooth connectivity and flexible partitions. Lufthansa is calling this “Premium XXL,” which… I’m not sure if that’s supposed to describe the seat, or if Lufthansa is taking some liberties on a fresh Grindr profile, somehow turning Vantage XL into Premium XXL.

    In a recent development, as A380s are reconfigured, the business class cabin is shrinking in size by 10 seats, going from 78 seats to 68 seats. First class continues to have eight seats, premium economy continues to have 52 seats, and economy continues to have 371 seats.

    Recent findings suggest that it’s pretty cool to note how Lufthansa has reversed course on the A380. At the beginning of the pandemic, Lufthansa grounded its fleet of Airbus A380s, and the intent was that these planes would be retired, and would only reenter service “in the event of an unexpectedly rapid market recovery.”.

    It has been revealed that with the strong recovery we’ve seen in transatlantic leisure demand, the airline made the decision to start bringing back Airbus A380s as of the summer of 2023, and eight of the initial 14 are now back in service (six of them were sold). At first, the return of the A380s was mostly described as a temporary measure, in light of delayed Boeing 777-9 deliveries. The airline didn’t commit to keeping these planes around in the long run, though that changed over time.

    It has been revealed that in recent years it has become clear that the A380 will have a long term place in Lufthansa’s fleet. Clearly this investment in the business class product reflects that.

    Lufthansa of course has its newly introduced Allegris cabins, including the new Allegris business class and new Allegris first class. These cabins debuted on newly delivered Airbus A350-900s, and we’re also seeing them on newly delivered Boeing 787-9s (though without first class).

    So why is Lufthansa not installing its fresh Allegris seats on the A380s? Well, I’d assume it comes down to a couple of factors. The biggest reason is quite straightforward — Lufthansa has had a really tough time getting its new Allegris seats certified, and these seats need to be certified on each individual aircraft. The idea is that by picking an “off the shelf” product, these seats are already certified, and therefore the airline could actually rely on getting them into service immediately.

    Second of all, I imagine that given the narrower fuselage of the A380 upper deck, it might’ve required even more complicated customization to fit the new Allegris seats up there.

    For once, I’d say Lufthansa made a wise decision by just picking a generic product for its A380s. I think the big mystery is why Lufthansa just didn’t do this for its other planes, to avoid this entire mess. Separately, Lufthansa is reconfiguring its Boeing 747-8s, in a complicated two-part process. Initially, we’ll see the new Allegris business class seats on the lower deck, while the same business class seats will remain on the upper deck.

    Lufthansa is wrapping up the process of introducing a new business class product on its Airbus A380s. The first plane with new cabins entered service in April 2026. While the initial plan was for all planes to be reconfigured as of the middle of 2027, it looks like that project will instead wrap up by December 2026, which is amazing.

    Industry observers note that rather than installing the new Allegris business class seats, the airline is instead installing a more generic product, the Thompson Aero Vantage XL seat, which is a significant improvement over the product you’ll otherwise find on these jets. As planes are reconfigured, business class capacity is being reduced by 10 seats, from 78 to 68.

    According to recent reports, lufthansa sure is all over the place when it comes to modernizing its cabins. Either way, this change is good to see.

    #6917. Why The GCAP Is The Only 6th-Generation Fighter Jet The Rest Of The World Can Actually Buy

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1463 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Why The GCAP Is The Only 6th-Generation Fighter Jet The Rest Of The World Can Actually Buy

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1463 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that in June 2026, Germany unveiled it was withdrawing from the FCAS 6th-generation fighter jet project with France and Spain.
    • It has been revealed that it is also being designed explicitly with an eye to exports.
    • Even so, there is discussion in Washington over whether the US aerospace industry has the bandwidth to develop two next-generation fighters side by side.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that in June 2026, Germany unveiled it was withdrawing from the FCAS 6th-generation fighter jet project with France and Spain. This left the GCAP/Tempest as the only credible European-led sixth-generation fighter jet program. The GCAP intends to be a reasonably heavy sixth-generation air superiority fighter jet built with an emphasis on multirole missions.

    It has been revealed that it is also being designed explicitly with an eye to exports. Developing a true sixth-generation fighter jet that functions as part of a fully integrated networked kill chain is now so complicated and so expensive that it can strain any nation's aerospace industry to the breaking point (with the possible exceptions of the US and China).

    Even so, there is discussion in Washington over whether the US aerospace industry has the bandwidth to develop two next-generation fighters side by side. Some advocate delaying the F/A-XX until after the F-47 is more developed.

    Fighter jet purchases are high-profile political affairs that can become politically heated quickly. This is often seen in South America and now in Canada, on the topic of purchasing US fighter jets (vs Swedish Gripens). Many countries do not wish to purchase US fighter jets for geopolitical reasons.

    Indonesia is an extreme example of a country exploring purchasing fighter jets from half a dozen countries to ensure no country has too much control over its fighter jet fleet (through spare parts and software updates). It has indicated that Turkish KAAN fighters would need to be free from US ITAR restrictions, a very tall ask.

    A range of factors, from Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014 to the passage of CAASTA in 2017 to the sanctions of 2022, have contributed to Russia's fighter jet export market collapsing. It has become infeasible for dozens of countries, including all NATO member Eastern European countries, to purchase Russian fighters.

    Indeed, Serbia said it was infeasible to purchase Russian fighters and so opted for French Rafales. Elsewhere, China is emerging on the stage as a serious export market for higher-end fighter jets. However, while some countries like Egypt, the UAE, and Argentina have openly touted purchasing Chinese fighters, only Pakistan has done so (J-10Cs and possibly upcoming J-35s).

    Industry observers note that many African countries and others have purchased lower-end Chinese fighters or advanced trainers. For many countries, purchasing Chinese fighters remains geopolitically complicated and is out of the question for non-aligned countries like Vietnam and India.

    It has been revealed that being developed by the UK, Italy, and Japan, the GCAP offers an alternative to the US, China, and Russia that can be more geopolitically salient for many countries. This is somewhat similar to how Canadians are at the moment viewing the Saab Gripen. It's not an 'enemy' Chinese or Russian fighter, but it's not fully American either.

    Industry observers note that australia, Saudi Arabia, and India have expressed interest in GCAP and the collapse of FCAS has reduced their options. It has also opened the door to the possibility of Germany (and possibly Spain) joining the program in some capacity. It would be a major boon for the GCAP if Germany were to join, as the trio (and particularly the UK) is presently struggling with financing the ambitious program by itself.

    Another crucial aspect is that any country can market its fighter jet as whatever generation they like. Pakistan has promoted later JF-17 variants, particularly the Block III, as possessing capabilities associated with 4.5-generation fighters (sometimes 4.5 'plus'). Sukhoi's marketing suggested its proposed Su-75 Checkmate low-cost fighter would be a fifth-generation fighter rivaling the F-35.

    In a recent development, fighter jet generation labels are part marketing, part clickbait, and part useful. The engineering of a next-generation aircraft is less about visible features (such as tailless vs large vertical stabilizers) and more about internal features (thermal management, sensor fusion, and networking).

    Without Germany, serious analysts do not think France will have the capacity to develop a fully-fledged sixth-generation fighter jet alone. France's Dassault has said it looks to go it alone and develop a next-generation fighter, although analysts expect this to be a lighter-weight, less ambitious carrier-based aircraft and closer to something like a fifth-generation 'plus' fighter.

    It has been revealed that perhaps a more important question is what Germany will do. Germany could partner with Sweden (and/or Spain) and develop a sixth-generation fighter jet that could compete with the GCAP. Even if it does, the GCAP has a head start, although such a jet could compete with GCAP sometime in the 2040s.

    Planned to be in service in 2035.

    Prototype/demonstrator flying, three-engined.

    Germany could throw its weight behind the GCAP, or another option could be for it to purchase more F-35s and focus on developing advanced teaming combat drones. Other programs, like South Korea's KF-21 and Turkey's KAAN fighter jet, are 4.5-generation fighter jets with low-observable characteristics.

    It has been revealed that these countries have aims to introduce later block upgrades to make them closer to fifth-generation jets. But they are not likely to compete in the GCAP's segment directly. Sweden could theoretically go it alone and develop a next-generation successor to the Saab Gripen, but it would likely be much less ambitious than the GCAP.

    According to recent reports, for now, the primary advanced frontline fighter jet the US offers on the export market is the F-35. In practice, in the late 2030s and 2040s, it could be a future F-35 Block 5 that will be the primary export competitor to the GCAP, although this is somewhat speculative. A future F-35 Block 5 could be a fifth-generation 'plus' fighter or thought of as a fifth-generation fighter with sixth-generation characteristics.

    Sources indicate that the primary 6th-generation jet the US is developing is the F-47. This is intended as the tip of the spear air dominance fighter. Its niche role is seen in how few the Air Force states it wants to purchase (185+), around a tenth of its program of record for the F-35A. The F-47 is designed to replace the F-22 and complement the F-35.

    Importantly, it is designed for USAF requirements without much regard for export air force requirements (unlike the GCAP and the F-35). In March 2025, US President Donald Trump noted a downgraded version of the F-47 would be available for export, although this is not his Administration's decision to make.

    It is the decision of later administrations. The export ban on the F-22 provides precedent for a future export ban. Even less is known about the Navy's F/A-XX, and it is possible land-based variants could be attractive on the export market (like the Hornet/Super Hornet were), but again, this is speculative.

    Sources indicate that as stated, many countries have geopolitical concerns with purchasing Chinese and Russian fighters. But there are other issues. One is that China has imposed an export ban on its high-end J-20 Mighty Dragon, much like the US and its F-22. This offers a precedent that China might be reluctant to export its leading next-generation fighter (possibly the J-36), but may be willing to export lower-level jets (such as the J-50).

    The US and China are the only two countries large enough to comfortably develop sixth-generation fighter jets exclusively for their own needs. Other countries like Russia, Japan, the UK, and France are forced to partner with other countries to spread the burden and/or design the aircraft for export in mind.

    As a rule, export jets need to be multirole, and able to fill many missions for smaller air forces. The French 'omnirole' Rafale is a great example. For Russia, there is another issue. It doesn't appear to have a credible sixth-generation fighter program. The last major upgrade from Rostec on the MiG-41/PAK DP (often termed a fifth-generation 'plus' interceptor) was in 2021.

    There is also no evidence that the program is a fully funded program with full state backing and commitment. Instead, it appears Russia is focusing on producing its mature Su-30/34/35 series, developing russified commercial aircraft, and maturing its Su-57 Felon.

    For now, it seems the GCAP/Tempest is the world's only credible, fully-funded sixth-generation program designed as a multirole platform useful to a range of air forces. The US F-47 appears highly niche, and the US's willingness to export the jet remains questionable. Before the US banned the highly specialized F-22, Japan, Israel, and Australia were considered three of the very few potential customers.

    Industry observers note that the GCAP remains the most ambitious next-generation program for the export market with committed funding. The first demonstrator is now being built by BAE Systems and is expected to fly in 2027. Japan remains adamant that it wants the jet to be in service by 2035, which would easily make it the first non-US and non-Chinese sixth-generation fighter to enter service.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, I’d like to think that I’m pretty understanding of airlines, and how they can fall short.
    • Industry observers note that at the same time, sometimes there are situations where airlines act in a way that feels to me a little like theft.
    • Several weeks ago, I booked a ticket on Tunisair in business class from Tunis (TUN) to Marseille (MRS).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, I’d like to think that I’m pretty understanding of airlines, and how they can fall short. The airline industry is incredibly complex and low margin, and sometimes consumers have unrealistically high expectations, while not acknowledging the real cost and challenges of running an airline. Buying a ticket on a flight is more like buying a ticket on Amtrak than buying a night at a Four Seasons, and you should adjust expectations accordingly.

    Industry observers note that at the same time, sometimes there are situations where airlines act in a way that feels to me a little like theft. Readers often share these stories with me, and I write about them when I can. Now I’d like to share my own story….

    Several weeks ago, I booked a ticket on Tunisair in business class from Tunis (TUN) to Marseille (MRS). A few days before the flight I received an email from Tunisair informing me that I had been downgraded. As it turns out, it was because my flight was swapped to a wet leased plane, in an all-economy layout.

    Sources indicate that the email informed me of this change without actually acknowledging it was a downgrade. Instead, the email was in French, and it translated to “we are writing to inform you that your flight reservation has undergone changes.” And the only reference to the downgrade was that the fare class only revealed as being “Y,” which obviously isn’t business class.

    There was zero other proactive communication from the airline about the incident, and I flew the flight in economy. The airline of course acted as if nothing happened, and there was no mention of how to request downgrade compensation, or anything like that.

    After the flight, I submitted a request with customer service, asking for a refund for the fare difference. Making that request was a challenge in and of itself, because the customer service form is in French, and is not at all intuitive.

    Recent findings suggest that but anyway, it has been weeks, and I haven’t heard back. I’m a bit conflicted here. I try not to abuse credit card disputes, but you typically only have 60 days to file a dispute. So am I at the point where I should just file a dispute, or how would one handle that?

    In a recent development, as I said above, I try to be pretty understanding of airlines, and recognize how many different scenarios there are. Just in terms of doing business ethically, I do feel like there should be a proactive refund offer if the airline is informing you in advance that you won’t be getting the product that you paid for. I mean, if you can inform me that I’ve been downgraded, you can also process some sort of a refund.

    According to recent reports, we’ve become desensitized to this kind of service level with airlines, but I’m trying to come up with a comparison. I guess it would be like buying premium tickets to a sporting event, being informed in advance that you’ll be given worse seats, and then customer service just not responding to you for weeks on end.

    If you managed to take my money, surely you can also manage to give it back if you can’t give me the thing I paid for, no?

    Tunisair informed me days before a flight that I had been downgraded (as it turns out, due to an aircraft swap), though there was no offer a refund for a fare difference, or anything. Weeks ago I sent an email to customer service asking for a refund for the fare difference, but I haven’t heard back.

    It just strikes me as really unethical to take someone’s money for an experience you’re not going to offer, and then not have a way to get a refund in a reasonable timeframe. I know airlines hate when people file credit card disputes, but when you’re approaching the 60-day mark with no response, what is one supposed to do?

    Am I the only one who thinks it’s ridiculous to proactively downgrade a customer, but then make getting a refund such a runaround?

    What Republicans don’t know about Black voters’ resilience cost them

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1010 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sen.-elect Scott Colom speaks during a victory rally at Tougaloo College on Nov.
    • Industry observers note that the campaign of Mississippi’s Sen.-elect Scott Colom was rightfully praised for its clever and brutal ads.
    • In a recent development, however, it was fitting that the Democrat’s closing message traded the edge for a solemn reminder of who and what brought him so far on his journey to his election as Mississippi’s first Black U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen.-elect Scott Colom speaks during a victory rally at Tougaloo College on Nov. 11. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images).

    Industry observers note that the campaign of Mississippi’s Sen.-elect Scott Colom was rightfully praised for its clever and brutal ads. The “pick another protein” spot will forever be stuck in the brains of a huge swath of Americans, especially Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith. She underestimated Colom and his team, and will soon be an ex-senator.

    In a recent development, however, it was fitting that the Democrat’s closing message traded the edge for a solemn reminder of who and what brought him so far on his journey to his election as Mississippi’s first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction.

    The ad delivered an all-American lesson about history, born of bravery and sacrifice.

    Filmed at the Jackson, Miss., home of slain civil rights leader Medgar Evers, the ad featured Colom recounting the story of Evers, a World War II veteran who survived Normandy, only to be shot in the back by a racist assassin, resentful that a Black man dared to exercise his rights as a citizen in the country he fought for.

    “He was killed for helping Mississippians vote,” Colom said. “On Tuesday, use your vote and honor everyone who died for that right.”.

    In a state where voting is still racially polarized, it was clear that Colom would not win over a majority of white voters; he won an estimated 25 percent, better than Democrats in recent elections and cutting into Trump’s margins, but certainly not a path to victory.

    According to recent reports, black voters in Mississippi made the difference, as they often have. With their allies in the cause of justice, they heeded the call. They indicated up despite the state’s stringent and often confusing voting restrictions, purges of the voting rolls engineered by Republican Secretary of State Michael Watson (who used unverified data from a credit bureau), and the U.S. Supreme Court Louisiana v. Callais decision that led to a wave of Southern states breaking up Black-majority districts.

    When the Mississippi purges resulted in “affidavit ballots” that required verification to count, as The Washington Post reported, young Black women tracked down those voters, one by one, to do everything they could to ensure voters’ efforts were not in vain.

    Black voters mattered in states all over the country, but especially in the South, where low turnout has plagued Democrats, particularly in midterm elections.

    Recent findings suggest that keisha Lance Bottoms was elected the first Black female governor in the country in Georgia, where Democrats won up and down the ballot. Newly elected senators Annie Andrews in South Carolina and James Talarico of Texas campaigned for and earned support from Black voters with proposals that rose above platitudes. And don’t sleep on North Carolina, where voters flipped seats the GOP tried to gerrymander into a hardened majority. The sight of hundreds of students from HBCU NC A&T State University, denied a campus early voting site, marching to the polls, must have made the ancestors smile.

    In Florida and Louisiana, where Democrats had little financial support and lost their statewide races, Black voters brought them tantalizingly close to victory and energized for the contests to come.

    I still don’t expect Republicans to give up the election shenanigans, done in the name of “election integrity” and color blindness but in reality designed to demoralize as much as suppress. Why try to win over a diverse electorate with an inclusive, policy-driven message when manipulating Black-majority districts can still work?

    The number of Black U.S. House members in the next session of Congress will fall, offset by a few Democrats who survived in redrawn districts, including Shomari Figures of Alabama and Don Davis of North Carolina.

    But you can’t redistrict a state, and you can’t skip town halls and expect tradition, support for the Confederacy and an “R” after your name to forever save you — the Hyde-Smith playbook.

    Recent findings suggest that "I blocked Scott Colom from being a federal judge, and you blocked him from being U.S. senator," she bragged, too soon, on election night.

    Maybe she should have emphasized affordability, saving rural hospitals and serving all Mississippians, as Colom did.

    What did GOP officials in those Southern red states think they would accomplish by focusing on their base and ignoring everyone else in states they were supposed to be serving?

    Did they not pay attention in history class, or maybe they attended one of those post-integration private schools where an unedited version of America’s past might not have been on the lesson proposal?

    Did they believe that voters who remembered Evers, Fannie Lou Hamer, Vernon Dahmer and countless others would shrug and say “you win” when legislatures and elections officials quickly and cynically pounced to quiet their voices?

    That would be disrespectful to all the people who worked for, sometimes died for rights they knew they may never enjoy, yet had a belief in America and the rightness of their cause.

    Sources indicate that scott Colom and the Evers family remembered. He was emotional in his reaction, in an MS NOW interview, when asked about the statement from Reena Evers-Everette, daughter of Medgar and Myrlie Evers. “Their courage helped make this moment possible,” she said.

    Colum agreed: “I absolutely stand on their shoulders. And from the bottom of my heart, I’m going to do everything I can to make them proud.”.

    Post-election, he has been very gracious, saying that he intends to serve all Mississippians, including the woman whom I suspect would hit a different note if the election had turned in her favor.

    It has been revealed that I have no doubt Scott Colom means it. He knows who paid the price to get him this far.

    Mary C. Curtis has worked at The New York Times, The Baltimore Sun, The Charlotte Observer, as national correspondent for Politics Daily, and is a senior facilitator with The OpEd Project. She is host of the CQ Roll Call “Equal Time with Mary C. Curtis” podcast. Follow her on X @mcurtisnc3.

    I encourage travelers to think outside the box when it comes to the credit cards in their wallet. Just because a card doesn't seem like a fit for you on the surface doesn't mean that's actually the case.

    In a recent development, that rings true for me with the Hawaiian Airlines® World Elite Mastercard®. I've never flown with Hawaiian Airlines and don't have any concrete plans to in the near future, yet this card offers significant value to me.

    Let me walk through exactly why that is.

    The information for the Hawaiian Airlines World Elite Mastercard has been collected independently by The Points Guy. The card details on this page have not been reviewed or provided by the card issuer.

    According to recent reports, the Hawaiian Airlines Mastercard earns Atmos Rewards points, which can be redeemed for Hawaiian, Alaska, Oneworld and nonalliance partner flights. As someone who was declined for the earlier this year, I didn't have a great way to earn Atmos Rewards points prior to opening this card.

    I'm based in the Pacific Northwest, so flights on Alaska Airlines are a common feature of my travel plans. While I can book these with my American Airlines AAdvantage miles, I don't want to put all my eggs in one loyalty program, since that leaves my rewards vulnerable to future devaluations and other negative program changes.

    The Hawaiian Airlines Mastercard offers a compelling, easy-to-earn welcome bonus:.

    On top of that, I'll earn 3 points per dollar spent on eligible Hawaiian and Alaska purchases and 2 points per dollar spent on dining, gas and groceries.

    Without this card, my only way of earning Atmos Rewards points was via Bilt Points transferred from my Bilt account, which isn't a particularly efficient method.

    While this card's benefits are understandably focused on Hawaiian Airlines, there are ways to use them on Alaska flights, too. I'll receive two free checked bags whenever I'm flying either Hawaiian or Alaska as long as I book with my card, a nice perk considering mid-tier cards typically only offer your first checked bag free.

    Upon account opening, I became eligible for a one-time 50% companion discount for one round-trip main cabin fare between North America and Hawaii. This is redeemable on either Alaska or Hawaiian, but I must use it within 13 months of account opening.

    Some possible use cases I have in mind include inviting a friend to join me on a trip to Hawaii or offering it to them as a discount for a positioning flight to Hawaii and back as part of a larger Asia itinerary we take together.

    Each account anniversary, this card offers a $100 companion discount for a round-trip main cabin fare, also usable on Alaska or Hawaiian. Both discounts may be subject to additional terms.

    According to recent reports, while it's unfortunate that these companion discounts are limited to travel between Hawaii and North America, it's not surprising considering this is a Hawaiian Airlines-branded card. It's a good incentive for me to finally start seriously considering some of the trips I've had on my list.

    The or its more affordable sibling, the , are likely better first choices for Alaska flyers — and possibly Hawaiian Airlines flyers as well.

    In a recent development, both cards offer a more valuable free checked bag benefit, with the opportunity to check a free bag for yourself as well as up to six people on the same itinerary (when you pay with your card). You'll also get preferred boarding on both airlines, which the Hawaiian Airlines Mastercard doesn't offer.

    Sources indicate that the Summit comes with eight Alaska lounge passes every year, a major upside for those flying Alaska often enough to value lounge access. It also earns well on foreign purchases, earning 3 points per dollar spent.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that hyatt will bring its luxury Park Hyatt brand to Brisbane, Australia.
    • In a recent development, hyatt has announced prepares for the Park Hyatt Brisbane, marking the brand’s debut in Queensland.
    • According to recent reports, the hotel will occupy the top floors of one of the two towers of the 309 North Quay, a mixed-use development also containing luxury homes and retail outlets.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that hyatt will bring its luxury Park Hyatt brand to Brisbane, Australia. More Park Hyatt locations are always a good thing, but… well, let’s cover the details first.

    In a recent development, hyatt has announced prepares for the Park Hyatt Brisbane, marking the brand’s debut in Queensland. The hotel is expected to open in 2031, and will be located on the shores of the Brisbane River, at the western edge of the city’s central business district.

    According to recent reports, the hotel will occupy the top floors of one of the two towers of the 309 North Quay, a mixed-use development also containing luxury homes and retail outlets. For what it’s worth, the two buildings will have 51 floors and 56 floors. The hotel will have 201 guest rooms and suites, offering views of the river and skyline, along with 50 serviced apartments, for extended residence.

    Sources indicate that there are no additional details about the property yet. I do appreciate that the hotel will at least be at the top of a building, as that should make for some very nice views (I hate when hotels are part of tall buildings, but then take up the bottom floors, as that’s becoming increasingly common).

    While a 2031 opening is expected, I would definitely not count on that timeline sticking. Ground hasn’t even broken on this development, and these kinds of mixed-use developments tend to struggle with sticking to their planned timeline.

    Here’s how Tamara Lohan, Hyatt’s Global Brand Leader for Luxury, describes this:.

    “The Park Hyatt calling cards have always been iconic design and extraordinary addresses. Brisbane has the confidence and growing global pull to make it a natural home for the brand. When it opens, Park Hyatt Brisbane will become the fifth Park Hyatt hotel in the Pacific, joining hotels in Sydney, Melbourne, Canberra and Auckland, and a deliberate next step in growing the brand in the right places.”.

    There are no renderings of the property yet, beyond the below one of the overall 309 North Quay development.

    This will be the fourth Park Hyatt property in Australia, and the fifth in the South Pacific, complementing the properties in Auckland, Canberra, Melbourne, and Sydney. I don’t have the slightest clue what’s going on with the Canberra property, as my understanding is that it’s not up to Park Hyatt standards, so it’s marketed as “Hyatt Hotel Canberra – A Park Hyatt Hotel.” So it is a Park Hyatt, or is it not a Park Hyatt?

    It has been revealed that world of Hyatt is my favorite major hotel loyalty program (though the lead is narrowing as of late), and Park Hyatt is probably my favorite Hyatt brand. 15 years ago, the brand got me really excited, because it had some really spectacular properties. But it just feels like the brand is sort of losing steam, especially when you compare the difference in trajectory between Park Hyatt and Waldorf Astoria. My frustration with Park Hyatt comes down to two things.

    First, the brand just seemingly can’t pick up many “flagship” properties, or at least can’t maintain them. Look at the world’s biggest business markets and most iconic cities — we’re talking Hong Kong, London, New York, Paris, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo, etc. There are no Park Hyatts in places like Hong Kong or Singapore, and the ones that have historically been pretty iconic just fall short of actually being the top properties in their cities:.

    Sources indicate that the area where Park Hyatt has been doing well in recent times is in secondary cities, at least in comparison to the above. And this isn’t meant to be shade — I’d much rather hang out in Auckland or Kuala Lumpur than in London or New York (take your pitchforks elsewhere!), but there’s no denying that any true luxury hotel brand wants to have world class properties in those primary cities.

    I just feel like as of late, Waldorf Astoria’s trajectory has been way more impressive than Park Hyatt’s, and I’m not sure what exactly is driving that. I feel like owners just aren’t as into developing Park Hyatts as they used to be. Is there a single Park Hyatt in the pipeline where I think “oh, this is going to be a best-in-class property in a major market?” I can’t think of any….

    Sources indicate that the Park Hyatt brand is coming to Brisbane, Australia, with a hotel expected to open in 2031. The 201-key property will be located on the top floors of a mixed-use development, which will also contain apartments and retail.

    It’s cool to see more Park Hyatts in the pipeline, and I don’t want to knock the brand for expanding to more markets. I’m just disappointed that the Park Hyatt brand can’t pick up any steam in the biggest cities, in terms of delivering an actually competitive experience.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    President Donald Trump meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin ahead of trilateral talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

    President Donald Trump's visit to China for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit featured an elaborate welcome, warm exchanges with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and a declaration of American technological dominance on Chinese soil.

    The gathering in Shenzhen culminated in the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia, with nuclear arms reductions and the war in Ukraine among the complications on the table.

    Here are some of the standout moments from Trump's visit.

    XI BREAKS PROTOCOL TO PERSONALLY WELCOME TRUMP AHEAD OF HISTORIC TRILATERAL SUMMIT AND MORE TOP HEADLINES.

    Trump declared the United States the world leader in "superintelligence" during remarks at the summit Thursday, making the assertion in one of China's major technology hubs.
