    Fun & Creative Airline Callsigns, From Shamrock To Starwalker

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1330 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Here’s a fun topic for aviation geeks (so if you’re not one, feel free to skip this post)….
    • When pilots and air traffic controllers communicate, they have a callsign that they use to be identified.
    • In general aviation, that callsign is just the aircraft’s registration code, so it’s always the same for a particular aircraft.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Here’s a fun topic for aviation geeks (so if you’re not one, feel free to skip this post)….

    When pilots and air traffic controllers communicate, they have a callsign that they use to be identified.

    In general aviation, that callsign is just the aircraft’s registration code, so it’s always the same for a particular aircraft. For example, if the plane has the registration code N111PG, it would be spoken as “November One One One Papa Golf.”.

    In a recent development, meanwhile for commercial aircraft, the callsign consists of a organization identifier plus the flight number. In some cases that company identifier is simply the company’s name, while in other cases, a different callsign is used. For example, for American, Delta, and United, the company identifier is simply the airline name, so American flight 100 would be spoken as “American 100.”.

    In some situations, airlines choose callsigns that are different from the company name, and this can be for a variety of reasons. Callsigns need to be approved by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), with some important considerations:.

    While most airlines simply use their name as their callsign, there are also some airlines that don’t, and there are some names that I find to be particularly fun. In this post, I’d like to share my favorite airline callsigns, with a little backstory on how they were chosen (as I understand it). In no particular order….

    It has been revealed that aer Lingus’ callsign is “Shamrock,” and that’s because the shamrock is the national symbol of Ireland. It’s a key part of the airline’s corporate identity, down to the shamrock being featured on the tails of Aer Lingus planes.

    Recent findings suggest that british Airways’ callsign is “Speedbird,” and I’d argue it’s perhaps the most iconic callsign out there. The origin of this dates back to British Airways’ predecessor, Imperial Airways, which used the stylized bird logo. British Airways has been using the callsign since it was founded in 1974 (as a combination of predecessors).

    While this is of course a creative callsign, it has a practical use as well. “British Airways” would’ve been too long of a callsign, and “British” would’ve likely been too generic. For example, British Midland (which ended up being merged into British Airways) used “Midland” as its callsign, to avoid confusion.

    Republic Airways’ callsign is “Brickyard,” and it’s probably the coolest callsign you’ll find at an airline in the United States. The callsign is a tribute to the manufacturer’s headquarters in Indianapolis, also home to the Indianapolis Motor Speedway. The course was initially paved with three million bricks, and nicknamed “The Brickyard.”.

    For those not familiar, Republic operates flights on behalf of the regional subsidiaries of the major US carriers, so this is among the most common callsigns you’ll hear on air traffic control frequencies in the US.

    Sources indicate that PSA Airlines’ callsign is “Blue Streak,” and after Republic, it’s probably the coolest callsign you’ll find at an airline in the United States. The story behind this callsign is definitely a blast from the past. In the 1980s, PSA’s predecessor was Jetstream International Airlines, and it operated commuter flights as a Piedmont Commuter feeder carrier.

    The carrier’s planes had a white fuselage with a prominent blue stripe along it, intended to match Piedmont Airlines’ livery, and that’s where it all started.

    Sources indicate that for those not familiar, PSA operates flights on behalf of the regional subsidiaries of the major US carriers, so this is also a very common callsign that you’ll hear. Given the lack of blue stripes nowadays, the callsign does tend to cause some confusion!

    China Airlines’ callsign is “Dynasty.” It’s my understanding that the Taiwan-based carrier had to choose a non-obvious callsign both to avoid confusion (given the number of airlines with “China” in their name), and also with the intent of differentiating it from mainland China.

    In a recent development, so, where did the dynasty term come from? China Airlines uses this branding pretty widely, with its frequent flyer program even being named Dynasty Flyer, and it’s intended to reflect the history of Taiwan.

    Starlux Airlines’ callsign is “Starwalker.” The reason is because the “Starlux” callsign was already taken by Comlux Aruba, a tiny charter airline, before the Taiwanese airline was founded. Now, don’t ask me why Comlux Aruba has “Starlux” as its callsign, though!

    In a recent development, the reason Starlux ended up with “Starwalker” is presumably because the firm’s founder is a huge Star Wars fan, which is why many things about the airline have space branding. He’s also of course a huge aviation geek, and operates flights as a captain!

    South African Airways’ callsign is “Springbok.” The reason is because “South African” would be too long of a callsign, so they selected the springbok, which is the national animal of South Africa. The carrier has also used this in its branding over the years. For example, back in the 1950s, the airline used “Springbok Service” to describe its long haul, flagship flights.

    Atlas Air’s callsign is “Giant.” Huh, say what? For those not familiar, Atlas Air is a cargo and charter airline, and while it doesn’t operate regularly scheduled commercial flights, it is a big operation.

    The callsign is presumably a reflection of the company’s name coming from Greek mythology, where “Atlas” was a titan of great strength, so that may also explain the “giant” callsign. Now, it’s worth mentioning that Atlas also flies some pretty “giant” planes, as the world’s largest Boeing 747 operator, but I don’t think that’s the primary motivation.

    Sources indicate that kalitta Air’s callsign is “Connie.” For those not familiar, Kalitta Air is a cargo airline with a few dozen planes (most of which are Boeing 747s!). The callsign is named after the company’s founder, Conrad “Connie” Kalitta, who started the airline back in 1967, as Connie Kalitta Services.

    European Air Transport’s callsign is “Postman.” For context, this is one of DHL’s European subsidiaries operating cargo flights, so it’s a pretty fitting callsign, eh?

    Airlines have callsigns that they use to communicate with air traffic control. While most airlines simply use their name as their callsign, that’s not always the case. In some situations a different name has to be chosen for practical reasons, while in some cases airlines want to get creative. I love when airlines have some fun with this, so I figured it was worth a post.

    What’s your favorite airline callsign?

    • District Court for the District of Columbia made the statement Tuesday during a hearing brought by news organizations and an advocacy group seeking details about the search.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., speaks during a news conference at the Capitol last summer. Few details have emerged so far about the government’s search of her home earlier this fall. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    A judge stated he will order the release of some information about the federal investigation into Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., which included a search of her Washington house last month.

    Judge James Boasberg for the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia made the statement Tuesday during a hearing brought by news organizations and an advocacy group seeking details about the search. Boasberg ordered the government to provide him by Friday what could be disclosed in the case. He pointed to how investigators are handling the “speech or debate” clause immunity that Omar has as a sitting member of Congress.

    “This is purely legal questions, interesting questions, about the privilege, the extent of the privilege and how it would apply,” Boasberg remarked.

    The Constitution includes an immunity for members of Congress for the “speech or debate” they engage in as part of their jobs.

    Recent findings suggest that boasberg also directed the government to propose redactions to the as-yet secret docket. While he remarked next week’s expected disclosures would not include the 67-page document that investigators provided to justify the search, he left the door open to unsealing that down the road if the government closes the case or brings charges.

    Justice Department attorney Alessandra Serano argued against broad disclosures, calling it “very rare that a precharging, pre-indictment unsealing would happen.”.

    The high-profile nature of the investigation leaked into the courtroom Tuesday, as Boasberg cited statements by President Donald Trump and others about the investigation into Omar.

    “You have had administration officials, prominent ones, talking about the purpose of the investigation,” Boasberg said.

    Administration officials have accused Omar of committing immigration crimes for years, and Trump noted last month the DOJ was looking into Omar “strongly.” Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said on a recent podcast that investigators had served multiple search warrants and were investigating possible immigration fraud tied to when Omar entered the United States as a child.

    Separately, Boasberg said he may problem rulings in the coming weeks unsealing portions of other court cases tied to the investigation, including one brought by Omar herself earlier this month seeking the return of the items seized in the search.

    Industry observers note that the administration executed the search warrant in October, just a few weeks before the midterm elections. The timing of the search drew accusations of political bias from Democrats who claimed that the administration brought the case to sway the midterm elections.

    For years Trump has stated he wanted criminal charges to be brought against his political foes, including Omar and others in Congress.

    Industry observers note that an American Airlines flight, an Airbus A319 departing from Phoenix Sky Harbor International Airport (PHX), declared Mayday on Thursday shortly after takeoff. It happened after the crew on the trailing flight, operated by SkyWest Airlines, warned air traffic control (ATC) when they reportedly saw flames from one of the aircraft's engines.

    AA3230 was a scheduled flight departing from PHX to Portland International Airport (PDX). The flight promptly returned to Phoenix as the incident was unfolding.

    The pilots onboard the American flight bound for PDX had initially confirmed to ATC that the aircraft experienced hydraulic problems shortly after departure, and as a result, the flight would need to return to Phoenix.

    Moments later, according to Flightdrama, the crew came across the radio declaring 'Mayday, Mayday, Mayday' and requesting vectors to return to Phoenix (a specific compass heading which is assigned by local ATC that assists in guiding a pilot's flight path using surveillance data like radar).

    American confirmed the incident in a statement to Simple Flying late Thursday.

    Recent findings suggest that "American Airlines flight 3230 returned to Phoenix (PHX) due to a mechanical glitch. The aircraft landed safely, taxiied to the gate under its own power and was taken out of service to be inspected by our maintenance team. Customers deplaned normally and will re-depart this evening on a new aircraft. Safety is our top priority and we thank our team members for their professionalism and apologize to our customers for the disruption in their travel plans.".

    In a recent development, as the crew declared Mayday, ATC asked a series of questions, including whether the plane needed to burn off excess fuel. The pilots confirmed that 120 people were onboard. According to flight data from Simple Flying's Flight Tracker, AA3230 was expected to depart at 3:58 PM. The flight was briefly delayed and eventually pushed back from the gate in Phoenix to 4:14 PM, 16 minutes behind schedule. Taking off from the Arizona airport heading west, the jet spent a total of 20 minutes in the air before touching down safely in Phoenix at 4:34 PM.

    Upon arrival in Phoenix, the plane landed safely and taxied to the gate without assistance. The plane has since been removed from service, and passengers deplaned normally and were rebooked onto a replacement aircraft later that evening, which departed at 5:45 PM and arrived in Portland at 7:54 PM local time.

    In a recent development, the jet at the center of the incident was N703UW. According to ch-aviation, the 28-year-old A319-112 carries serial number 904 and was initially delivered to US Airways in 1998, then transferred to the American fleet following the airline's 2013 merger. The aircraft is configured with up to 132 seats in a two-class layout (including Domestic First and Main Cabin).

    According to recent reports, following the recent incident on the flight departing Phoenix, the aircraft remains grounded while further inspections are undertaken by the carrier's maintenance teams. The quick actions by the crew onboard, and the quick spotting by the following SkyWest service, helped relay vital information to air traffic control about the unfolding situation in Phoenix.

    The crew onboard AA3230 took rapid action, with clear coordination, to establish critical emergency details early, allowing ground and air teams to coordinate without delay and ensure the aircraft's prompt return to the ground and the safety of all occupants onboard.

    LATAM Unveils Newly introduced Airbus A321XLR Business Class Suites, Coming March 2027

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1138 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • LATAM has just unveiled the full interiors for its upcoming Airbus A321XLRs, which will make it the first carrier in South America to offer fully flat suites with direct aisle access on a narrow body aircraft.
    • Recent findings suggest that LATAM has 13 Airbus A321XLRs are on order, which are expected to enter service as of March 2027.
    • In a recent development, the airline intends to use these planes to open up fresh long haul markets, though it’s not yet clear out of which LATAM hubs the planes will fly.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    LATAM has just unveiled the full interiors for its upcoming Airbus A321XLRs, which will make it the first carrier in South America to offer fully flat suites with direct aisle access on a narrow body aircraft. These planes are expected to enter service in the coming months, so we won’t have to wait much longer to fly them!

    Recent findings suggest that LATAM has 13 Airbus A321XLRs are on order, which are expected to enter service as of March 2027. The A321XLR is the newly introduced long range, narrow body aircraft from Airbus, which stretches the capabilities of the A321 family.

    In a recent development, the airline intends to use these planes to open up fresh long haul markets, though it’s not yet clear out of which LATAM hubs the planes will fly. I suspect these planes will primarily be used for service to North America, or possibly for service from secondary cities in Brazil to Europe. Officially, for now the airline just claims these planes will be used to “strengthen connectivity between South America and more distant destinations.”.

    Earlier this year, LATAM’s CEO did drop some hints that the plane could fly from Lima (LIM) and Brasilia (BSB) to the United States, and from Fortaleza (FOR) to Europe, though no final decisions have been declared.

    We can expect LATAM to offer an all-new passenger experience (by the carrier’s standards) onboard the Airbus A321XLRs. The airline plans to configure the planes with a total of 174 seats, including:.

    Throughout the plane, passengers can expect the Panasonic Astrova entertainment system, with over 2,300 hours of content, including 330 movies and 1,200 TV shows. Bluetooth audio will also be available at all seats, so that passengers can connect to their own headphones. The A321XLR will also be equipped with SES Wi-Fi, with LATAM Pass members getting complimentary browsing or messaging, depending on their membership tier and ticket type.

    LATAM’s A321XLR business class will feature the Thompson Aero VantageSOLO product. So there will be 12 herringbone seats in a 1-1 configuration, with seats spread across six rows. This means all seats will have direct aisle access and doors. Business class seats will feature 19″ 4K OLED screens, AC power outlets, USB-C charging, and wireless charging.

    In a recent development, it also looks like the front row seats will be pretty special, as they’ll feature quite a bit of extra space, including a closet and wardrobe. It remains to be seen how the airline will monetize that extra space, if at all (maybe they’ll just be reserved for certain types of passengers?).

    Industry observers note that LATAM’s A321XLR business class will feature the Recaro R3 product. So there will be 162 seats in a 3-3 configuration, with six rows having extra legroom, and 21 rows having standard legroom. Economy class seats will feature 13″ 4K OLED screens, as well as USB-C outlets.

    The A321XLR is impressive for its range, and it’s understandable that the economics of such a small plane for long haul flying can be challenging. As a result, we’re really seeing airlines try to maximize capacity as much as possible, and this is also leading to so many airlines having very similar premium products on planes.

    LATAM will have herringbone seats on the A321XLR, just like… well, all current operators that use this primarily as a long haul aircraft, with the exception of Aer Lingus.

    For those keeping track at home, the Thompson Aero VantageSOLO product is what you’ll find in JetBlue’s Mint business class on select A321neo/LR aircraft, and it’s also what you’ll find in Iberia’s A321XLR business class.

    While American’s A321XLR business class looks similar, it’s based on the Collins Aerospace Aurora seating platform, and that’s also what Air Canada has selected. Meanwhile United’s A321XLR business class also looks similar, but is based on the Elevate Altitude platform.

    Admittedly these planes all have better business class products than we found on long haul Boeing 757s years ago (the most direct replacement), and the tech is also greatly updated. That being noted, as a passenger experience geek, this sure is a boring plane… “you get a herringbone seat, you get a herringbone seat, you get a herringbone seat, everyone gets a herringbone seat!”.

    While not quite A321XLRs, credit to ITA Airways’ A321neo business class and Etihad’s A321LR business class for having reverse herringbone seats.

    To LATAM’s credit, I will say that the cabin finishes look gorgeous, so I hope they look as nice in real life as they do in renderings.

    In early 2027, LATAM expects to start taking delivery of the Airbus A321XLR, which the airline plans to use to grow into new markets. The airline has now revealed what we can expect onboard these planes, and it includes herringbone seats with direct aisle access and doors in business class.

    Recent findings suggest that ultimately the cabin looks sleek, and it’s cool to see this in South America, where no other airline is currently offering such an experience. But still, it’s hard to get too excited when so many airlines are introducing a similar product.

    LATAM in general deserves credit for the extent to which it’s elevating the passenger experience in Latin America, as we’ve seen the airline introduce two fresh wide body business class products over the past several years.

    What do you make of LATAM’s new A321XLR business class?

    #6905. Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited Card Review: Is The $295 Fee Worth It?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 15m • 📚 Deep Dive (2934 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited Card Review: Is The $295 Fee Worth It?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 15 min read (2934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~15 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Graphite™ Business Cash Unlimited Card launched in March 2026.
    • It has been revealed that however, there are some things that could make this card worthwhile, including a potentially lucrative welcome offer, a solid return on spending, and some credits that can help offset the annual fee.
    • This post is my in-depth Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited review.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Graphite™ Business Cash Unlimited Card launched in March 2026. On the surface, the card sounds rather uncompetitive — it has a $295 annual fee (Rates & Fees), and offers “just” 2% cash back on everyday spending, with limited bonus categories.

    It has been revealed that however, there are some things that could make this card worthwhile, including a potentially lucrative welcome offer, a solid return on spending, and some credits that can help offset the annual fee. If your business spends a lot, you value having an Amex, and you just want to earn simple cash back without a complex rewards structure, this could be a good option.

    This post is my in-depth Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited review. Is the card worth it, and if so, under what circumstances? And what are the best alternatives?

    Link: Learn more about the Graphite™ Business Cash Unlimited Card.

    Before I get into my Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited review, let me briefly summarize the key details of the card:.

    Beyond that, here are what I consider to be some of the major pros and cons of the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited:.

    It has been revealed that with the above out of the way, let’s look at the various aspects of the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited, from the welcome offer, to the fees, to the rewards structure, to the other perks. This card is fairly straightforward, so there’s not all that much to understand, for better or worse.

    The Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited currently has a welcome offer where you can earn as high as $2,000 cash back after spending $50,000 within the first six months on eligible purchases. Reward Dollars can be redeemed as statement credits to offset transactions, or as a payment method for Amazon purchases.

    Given that the card ordinarily offers at least 2% cash back, that means spending $50,000 could earn you a minimum of $3,000 (if offered the full bonus amount), equivalent to 6% cash back on that amount of spending, which is solid.

    Admittedly the spending requirement is big (it averages out to $8,333 per month over the course of six months), but I do think businesses that spend a lot might find this to be achievable. Furthermore, it’s nice that you have six months to complete the spending requirement, while many other cards give you only three months to reach the spending requirement.

    If you’re applying for the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited, be aware of Amex’s general restrictions on applying for cards, including the “once in a lifetime rule.” That means you’re not eligible for the welcome offer on the card if you’ve already had this card, though you are potentially eligible for the bonus if you’ve had other Amex cards.

    Anecdotally, I find Amex business cards to be quite easy to get approved for. I also love how with Amex, you can know if you’ll be approved with no credit score impact — the hard pull only happens after you’re told if you’re approved, and you accept the offer.

    Also keep in mind that if you’re concerned about staying under Chase’s 5/24 limit, applying for an Amex business card won’t count toward that, since it doesn’t show up on your personal credit report in that way.

    Sources indicate that when it comes to credit score, there’s not a consistent credit score you need to get approved for the card, as it’s one of only many factors that determines eligibility. Personally, I’d hope to have a score in the “good” to “excellent” range, ideally 700+ points. However, people with lower scores have been approved, and people with higher scores have been rejected.

    The Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited has an annual fee of $295 (Rates & Fees), which is definitely on the steep side, especially given the relatively narrow appeal of the credits offered on the card, which require a lot of spending.

    With the card’s 2% cash back rewards structure, you’d essentially recoup the annual fee (in terms of rewards) after $14,750 in spending.

    The Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited has an authorized user fee of $95 for the first 5 cards, and a $95 annual fee for each thereafter (Rates & Fees), though you can also get a no annual fee Employee Business Expense Card with no additional fee. Still, that’s a rather steep authorized user fee for a card that doesn’t actually offer many incremental perks. You can add up to 99 employee cards to your account.

    Recent findings suggest that the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited has no preset spending limit. The idea is that this gives you flexibility in ways that traditional credit cards don’t. The amount you can spend adapts based on factors such as your purchase, payment, and credit history. Rather than having a set limit, you could grow your purchasing power the more you consistently use your card and regularly make payments.

    It has been revealed that in fairness, it is also worth mentioning that not having a preset spending limit can also lead to some declines if the amount you can charge decreases, so it’s a little less predictable than a regular credit card. However, I find that more often than not, it works in the favor of cardmembers.

    No Preset Spending Limit means your spending limit is flexible. Unlike a traditional card with a set limit, the amount you can spend adapts based on factors such as your purchase, payment, and credit history.

    In a recent development, in terms of its rewards structure, the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited offers a minimum of unlimited 2% cash back on eligible purchases. On top of that, the card offers 5% cash back on flights and prepaid hotels booked through American Express Travel® Online. Just to do some very basic math:.

    Industry observers note that all cash back on the card is earned as Reward Dollars, which can be redeemed as statement credits to offset transactions, or as a payment method for Amazon purchases. Unfortunately there are no other redemption options, so you couldn’t directly deposit the cash back into a business checking account, or anything like that.

    2% cash back on credit card spending is the “gold standard,” as I see it, so that’s excellent, and what everyone should be aiming for, at a minimum.

    It has been revealed that meanwhile the 5% cash back on Amex Travel might sound appealing, but there are some catches. If you can route travel spending that way, it’s a good option, but the catch is that you may sometimes find lower rates elsewhere, so there could be an opportunity cost to booking that way.

    Industry observers note that the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited offers up to $2,400 in American Express One AP® statement credits, after spending $250,000 on eligible purchases on the card in a calendar year. Statement credits will be applied to the monthly bill charged to the card for Amex’s accounts payable solution, One AP, for the following calendar year, and this includes an auto-renewing platform access fee.

    It has been revealed that american Express One AP® is an accounts payable solution that can help transform the way your business pays suppliers. With One AP, you can streamline your supplier invoice payments on a single platform and pay by virtual card, check, and ACH. Enrollment is required.

    This program charges a $200 monthly fee to pay vendors with non-cards, plus has a fee for checks and ACHs over a certain limit. So the $2,400 annual credit can potentially fully cover your monthly fee. While this is potentially a nice feature, keep in mind that many platforms already offer this as a built in feature at no extra cost, so it’s not really that special.

    Recent findings suggest that the Amex Graphite Business Cash Unlimited offers the Pay Over Time feature, whereby cardmembers can carry a balance with interest on eligible charges, up to the Pay Over Time limit. The way this works, eligible charges will automatically be added to a Pay Over Time balance, up to the Pay Over Time limit.

    You can choose to pay for these charges over time with interest, or you can pay your full balance each month, whichever is best for your business. You must pay in full any charge or a portion of a charge that is not added to a Pay Over Time balance.

    Sources indicate that personally, I recommend paying the balance in full each billing cycle if possible, to avoid interest charges, especially given how high they can be. However, I think it’s worth clarifying that the Pay Over Time option is possible, given that this isn’t a traditional credit card.

    It’s also worth emphasizing the difference between the Pay Over Time and the Pay In Full Limit. The latter could be an amount that has to be paid in full, and there’s no option to pay that over time with interest charges.

    The Amex Graphite Business Cash Card earns 2% cash back, and I consider that to be the minimum “gold standard” of credit card rewards. So the card’s rewards structure is perfectly fine. The 5% cash back on travel is also pretty limiting, given that you have to book through Amex.

    Recent findings suggest that I think the problem is the steep annual fee, given that there are also much more affordable (and even no annual fee) cards with that kind of a rewards structure. In fairness, Amex doesn’t have another business card earning unlimited 2% cash back. It’s just not a newly introduced concept more broadly, and there are lots of competing cards that I’d consider to be superior.

    In a recent development, so who should consider the card? As I see it, the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card is targeted at a specific demographic. This card could make sense for the following types of customers:.

    According to recent reports, I do truly think this is a niche product. But the idea is that if you’re a small business owner charging hundreds of thousands or millions of dollars on credit cards per year, that annual fee won’t make much of a difference.

    Still, I’d like to compare this to some other popular products, as I think there are other cards that may be a better fit for some other people.

    Perhaps the best direct comparison to the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card is The American Express Blue Business Cash® Card (learn more). The card has no annual fee (Rates & Fees) and offers 2% cash back on the first $50,000 spent every calendar year (and 1% cash back thereafter).

    According to recent reports, the upside here is obvious, as you’re earning 2% cash back with no fee. The downside is that the welcome offer is much smaller (though also with a smaller spending requirement), the card has foreign transaction fees, you’re capped at earning 2% cash back on the first $50,000 spent annually, and the card does have a preset spending limit.

    For a small business mostly spending money domestically, the Amex Blue Business Cash is a great alternative to the Amex Graphite Business Cash.

    It has been revealed that another potential alternative to the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card is The Blue Business® Plus Credit Card from American Express (learn more). The card has no annual fee (Rates & Fees) and offers 2x Membership Rewards points on the first $50,000 spent every calendar year (and 1x points thereafter).

    In a recent development, if you’re good at redeeming points, that’s a pretty incredible return, since based on my latest miles & points valuations, Amex points are worth 1.7 cents each, for a return of up to 3.4%. The downsides to the Amex Blue Business Plus are otherwise identical to those on the Amex Blue Business Cash — the welcome offer is much smaller (though also with a smaller spending requirement), the card has foreign transaction fees, you’re capped at earning 2x points on the first $50,000 spent annually, and the card does have a preset spending limit.

    So the card is either useful if $50,000 covers your annual business spending, or you’re willing to use another card after you hit that initial $50,000 spending cap.

    Speaking of premium Amex business cards, it’s also worth comparing the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card to the American Express® Business Gold Card (learn more). The Amex Business Gold has a $375 annual fee (Rates & Fees), and offers an incredible rewards structure (with up to 4x Membership Rewards points in select categories), plus statement credits that can greatly help offset the annual fee.

    As I see it, the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card is the better option if you value cash back and a straightforward rewards structure, while the Amex Business Gold is the better option if you can take advantage of the bonus categories, and are willing to put in the effort to maximize points.

    While the above comparisons are all to Amex cards, I think it’s also worth comparing the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card to the Capital One Spark Cash Plus (learn more), as it’s perhaps the most direct competitor.

    The card has a massive welcome offer of $2,000 cash back after spending $30,000 within the first three months (plus an additional $2,000 cash back bonus for every $500,000 spent during the first year), offers 5% cash back on select Capital One Business Travel purchases and 2% cash back with no caps and no foreign transaction fees on other purchases, and it has a $150 annual fee. Furthermore, the card offers an annual bonus of $150 if you spend at least $150,000 on the card in a calendar year, essentially rebating the annual fee.

    I do think the Capital One Spark Cash Plus is more compelling than the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card on balance, unless you specifically have a reason you’d like an Amex, or value the statement credits tied to spending $250,000 per year.

    I’d also like to compare the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card to the Ink Business Premier® Credit Card (learn more), as it’s another potentially lucrative cash back card.

    In addition to a massive welcome offer of $1,000 cash back after spending $10,000 within the first three months, the card offers 5% cash back on Chase Travel purchases, 2.5% cash back on purchases of $5,000 or more, and 2% cash back on all other purchases, with no foreign transaction fees, and it has a $195 annual fee. So if you have a business that frequently makes large purchases, the Chase Ink Business Premier could be a great alternative.

    Industry observers note that the Amex Graphite Business Cash Card has a $295 annual fee, and offers unlimited 2% cash back, with no preset spending limit, plus a large welcome offer. The card also offers up to $2,400 in American Express One AP® statement credits, after spending $250,000 on eligible purchases on the card in a calendar year.

    Ultimately I’d consider this to be a niche card. The card could be worth getting for the excellent welcome offer, and it could be worth it if you have a business that spends a huge amount, and values the lack of a preset spending limit, the card’s Amex branding, and/or the statement credits.

    Beyond that, though, I tend to think there are better options. If you’re not a huge spender, the Amex Blue Business Cash and Amex Blue Business Plus are excellent options. If you’re willing to maximize points and bonus categories, consider the Amex Business Gold. And if you’re looking for the best direct alternative that’s arguably more lucrative, consider the Capital One Spark Cash Plus.

    #6904. These incoming members of Congress have been here before

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1101 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    These incoming members of Congress have been here before

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1101 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that rep.-elect Chris Rabb, D-Pa., greets current members of Congress in the Capitol on Nov.
    • When Rep.-elect Chris Rabb first worked on Capitol Hill in the 1990s, it didn’t exactly inspire him to want to go into politics.
    • “I stated, ‘Oh, this is how the sausage is made?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that rep.-elect Chris Rabb, D-Pa., greets current members of Congress in the Capitol on Nov. 11. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    When Rep.-elect Chris Rabb first worked on Capitol Hill in the 1990s, it didn’t exactly inspire him to want to go into politics.

    “I stated, ‘Oh, this is how the sausage is made? I should be a vegan,’” the Pennsylvania Democrat recalled.

    Working for Carol Moseley Braun, the first Black woman elected as a U.S. senator, Rabb saw threats and “just vile things” directed at her.

    “My entrée to service behind the scenes was seeing voluminous amounts of violence, hate speech and death threats against my boss, and I thought to myself, ‘Why would anyone want to serve?’” he said.

    During his time in the state legislature starting in 2017, Rabb “fell in love with public service, despite the vitriol.” Now, the democratic socialist describes coming to Congress as “surreal,” as he succeeds retiring Rep. Dwight Evans in a deep-blue district based in West Philadelphia.

    Rabb is one of more than a dozen incoming members who have worked on the Hill before, ranging from interns to chiefs of staff and everything in between.

    Unlike some in the 100-plus-strong freshman class, they already know their way around the hallways. And Rabb has some advice for his new colleagues: “Treat your staff well. Take care of your staff; they’ll take care of you.”.

    Here are some of the former staffers who will join the House in January.

    A couple years ago, Killin was working as chief of staff to former second gentleman Doug Emhoff. But she started out on the Hill.

    “It is helpful to know, as I joke, where the bathrooms are, but I still feel like I have a lot to learn,” remarked the Army veteran, who unseated Republican Rep. Jeff Crank in a Colorado Springs-area district.

    She served as the top staffer for three House Democrats: Donna Shalala of Florida, Carolyn Maloney of Latest York and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez of Washington.

    “I’ve actually opened up two freshman offices, so it’s helpful to have done that before,” Killin noted.

    White will be just the third person in modern times to hold the job of nonvoting D.C. delegate. He replaces retiring Del. Eleanor Holmes Norton — also his former boss.

    Industry observers note that before his time on the D.C. Council, he worked as her legislative counsel, watching her navigate a role with limited power in her perennial fight for statehood.

    “I need to make sure I’m developing a national profile for this seat,” he said, vowing to continue the quest for full representation even as President Donald Trump seeks to exert more control over the District.

    One of just a few Republican women in the freshman class, Gruters mentioned she “never in a million years” imagined coming to Congress herself, despite her years as a staffer.

    She will replace retiring Rep. Vern Buchanan in Florida’s 16th District, after once serving as his operations director. She also worked as district director for Rep. Greg Steube, R-Fla.

    “I never thought this would be the path, but I’m honored to do it,” said Gruters, whose husband leads the Republican National Committee.

    Rogers added another title to his résumé last week: freshman class president.

    His fellow incoming Republicans tapped him for the role. Not so long ago, he was working for the Senate Judiciary Committee, fresh off a stint at the white-shoe law firm White & Case.

    In 2025 he served as general counsel for Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., and intends to keep pushing for a bill he helped draft that aims to crack down on foreign surrogacy contracts. “We are presently selling American children to China, our No. 1 adversary,” Rogers noted, describing it as “deplorable.”.

    Sources indicate that rogers will succeed retiring GOP Rep. Neal Dunn in the Florida Panhandle.

    García’s run for her boss’s seat drew controversy from the start. When Rep. Jesús “Chuy” García, D-Ill., waited to publicly announce his retirement until after the filing deadline in Illinois had already passed, critics blasted him for effectively boxing out other candidates and clearing the way for his chief of staff.

    It has been revealed that he faced a rare formal disapproval vote in the House over the move. But García has insisted she is more than a hand-picked successor, saying on her campaign website that she has “delivered solutions rooted in lived experience.”.

    #6902. Latest Update: How Chicago O’Hare's 8 Active Runways Handle More Than 2,000 Movements A Day

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1512 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Simpleflying ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: How Chicago O’Hare's 8 Active Runways Handle More Than 2,000 Movements A Day

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1512 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Simpleflying

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that it's well known that the busiest airport in the world is Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL).
    • Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD) is the world's busiest airport by aircraft movements, logging well over 2,000 per day, and the airport recorded over 857,000 aircraft movements in total throughout 2025.
    • The eight runways at ORD are oriented in two main directions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that it's well known that the busiest airport in the world is Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL). However, Atlanta is the world's busiest only by number of annual passengers, which is useful when measuring airline operations or evaluating operations in the terminal. Measuring aircraft movements (all aircraft takeoffs and landings), meanwhile, is useful for determining how much traffic the airfield receives. In other words, this reveals how many planes are actually operating out of the airport.

    Chicago O'Hare International Airport (ORD) is the world's busiest airport by aircraft movements, logging well over 2,000 per day, and the airport recorded over 857,000 aircraft movements in total throughout 2025. The airfield handles more aircraft than any other in the world, which means that it needs an efficient taxiway and runway system to accommodate so much traffic. One of ORD's most distinctive features is its runways, as it has eight in total, more than any other airport in the world.

    The eight runways at ORD are oriented in two main directions. In effect, there are six parallel runways running east-west, numbered as 9L/27R, 9C/27C, 9R/27L, 10L/28R, 10C/28C, and 10R/28L. In addition, there are also two parallel runways running from southwest to northeast, numbered 4L/22R and 4R/22L. The longer of the two, Runway 4R/22L, is only 8,075 feet (2,461 meters) long, and these two are only used during exceptionally strong crosswinds or unusual traffic flow.

    Sources indicate that most of the time, ORD operates like an airport with six parallel runways, which is an exceptionally efficient configuration. Air traffic controllers may run up to four parallel approaches with the airport's current layout, although this is not always done, and controllers often run two parallel departures as well. With the current runway layout, the airport is actually constrained more heavily by departures than arrivals, and Chicago could accommodate more flights than it currently sees.

    In a recent development, ORD's current runway configuration is relatively newly introduced, as construction of the airport's updated runways concluded in 2021. The project ended with the extension of Runway 9R/27R, while Runway 9C/27C is a new addition to the airport. Prior to the ORD improvement project, O'Hare had seven runways configured in a less efficient layout, and the new layout now allows for significantly more flights. This is more important now than ever as the airline's two home airports are rapidly growing.

    United Airlines is Chicago's hometown airline, as the airline has long been headquartered in the city and O'Hare is its largest hub. In addition, American Airlines has operated a substantial hub operation out of ORD for decades, standing as a firm number two at the airport. It is one of the most competitive markets in the US, even without Delta Air Lines, and the two airlines' operations at ORD make it one of the busiest airports, with actual traffic figures exceeding Atlanta.

    United Airlines mainly operates out of Terminal One at ORD, while some of its regional services operate out of Terminal Two. American Airlines' operations are based out of Terminal Three at ORD, while both airlines primarily send their international arrivals to Terminal Five, as this is right now the only terminal at ORD with a Federal Inspection Station (FIS). United Airlines currently holds just over 90 gates at ORD, whereas American Airlines holds over 60 gates at O'Hare after the most recent round of gate allocations.

    Sources indicate that for the summer 2026 schedule, United Airlines was running roughly 650 daily departures at its peak, which was over 100 more than it ran the prior summer. American Airlines operated over 500 daily departures during the 2026 summer season. Both operate a sizable domestic network out of O'Hare, along with some European services, and United even operates nonstop services to Tokyo. Notably, American and United's schedules were meant to be even larger, but they were trimmed after FAA-imposed flight caps at ORD.

    The recent runway improvement project at ORD significantly revised the layout of the airfield, creating a more efficient configuration that can accommodate more flights. Construction began in 2003 to update the runways, of which there were six at the time, arranged in a 'pinwheel' layout. The runways were set in different directions to accommodate various wind patterns, and most of them intersected with one another, an arrangement that reduced capacity as not all runways could be used at the same time.

    It has been revealed that across nearly two decades of work, ORD closed two runways, constructed four newly introduced ones, and extended two runways. The result is that there are now six parallel runways, with three located north and three located south of the terminal complex. This results in more crosswind departures and arrivals, but makes for significantly more efficient traffic flows. At any given point, controllers typically use three runways for arrivals, while two runways are often used for departures.

    Recent findings suggest that located at the north of the airfield, Runway 9L/27R can take arrivals from the north, while Runway 9C/27C takes some arrivals from the south and heavy aircraft. Runways 9R/27L and 10L/28R are the closest runways to the terminals and are used for departures, while Runway 10L/28R is also the airport's longest runway. In addition, Runway 10C/28C can be used for remaining arrivals from the south. Runway 10R/28L is also used for arrivals from the west, but the 28L side is used less often due to the proximity of Runway 4R/22L.

    The six parallel runways can operate in the common east-west flows with high capacity, especially because none of these runways intersect with one another. Meanwhile, for strong crosswind conditions, the airport also has Runway 4L/22R and 4R/22L. While Runway 4L/22R does intersect with Runways 9C/27C and 9R/27L, this runway is not used particularly often. Meanwhile, Runway 22L specifically is often used for departures during 'west flows', during which Runway 28L is generally not used.

    Recent findings suggest that throughout the years, United has been the number one at ORD, while American has been a solid number two. Post-COVID, however, United has gradually been growing its schedule closer to pre-pandemic levels, while American cut flights in 2022 and 2023. Still, even United wouldn't end up reaching pre-pandemic levels until 2026, when it planned a massive schedule of roughly 750 daily flights on average. This was over 200 more than its daily average in 2025, and significantly more than American's schedule, which was ambitious in itself.

    It has been revealed that united was essentially aiming to dump capacity into the market in an effort to push American out, and given how crucial the Chicago market is, American responded through significant growth of its own. The two airlines were looking at a bloodbath, which was also partially motivated by Chicago's gate allocation system that assigns gates based on usage. But with United planning up to 750 daily flights and American planning over 500 daily departures, it was starting to look like ORD would be taken beyond its limits.

    Sources indicate that the FAA instituted a flight cap that cut ORD's capacity to just over 2,700 takeoffs and landings per day, whereas airlines had planned over 3,000 for the 2026 summer season. The cap was instituted due to concerns about delays and congestion, but it hurt United significantly more than American, as the cap was determined based on ORD's 2025 summer schedule. United planned significantly more growth for 2026 than American did, which means that the two airlines are much closer than United had planned for.

    While ORD has an efficient runway layout, several taxiways are presently closed due to ongoing construction. As such, the airport frequently faces bottlenecks and delays with departing aircraft, in particular, clogging up taxiways. Pushbacks get delayed, which means that arriving planes don't have a place to park, leading air traffic controllers to send aircraft on extended taxi routes or to put them in the infamous 'penalty box' (technically the de-icing pad now), patiently waiting with the parking brake on until the gate opens up.

    Sources indicate that while ORD's runway projects are complete, the airport is undergoing a much larger modernization project. This includes a fresh Terminal Two (also known as the Global Terminal), which will accommodate international arrivals (currently, Terminal Five is the only one that can do so), as well as expansions to concourses at the airport's other terminals. In addition, ORD is revising its taxiway layouts for greater efficiency and to accommodate future terminal expansions.

    While there are elements of ORD's airfield design that are efficient and effective, the airport is also infamous for long taxi times and a lack of gate availability. During peak times, ramp controllers need to use a metering system to control the flow of aircraft entering the taxiways, while some of the runways are located far away from the core terminal area. Through the terminal projects and latest taxiways on the horizon, however, ORD should be much more capable of handling even higher flight volumes in the future.

    #6900. Tech Report: Supreme Court urged to defang ‘criminal trap’ that has sent Trump officials to prison

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1187 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foxnews ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Supreme Court urged to defang ‘criminal trap’ that has sent Trump officials to prison

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1187 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foxnews

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Abhi Kambli, Navarro's attorney, indicates a ruling in his favor could curb the 'weaponization' of congressional subpoenas by making contempt convictions harder to secure.
    • A Trump administration official who served four months in federal prison for defying a congressional subpoena is asking the Supreme Court to overturn his convictions in a case that could raise the bar for criminally prosecuting others who refuse to comply with Congress’s demands.
    • Peter Navarro, who was a senior trade advisor to President Donald Trump during his first administration, filed a petition with the Supreme Court last month.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Abhi Kambli, Navarro's attorney, indicates a ruling in his favor could curb the 'weaponization' of congressional subpoenas by making contempt convictions harder to secure.

    A Trump administration official who served four months in federal prison for defying a congressional subpoena is asking the Supreme Court to overturn his convictions in a case that could raise the bar for criminally prosecuting others who refuse to comply with Congress’s demands.

    Peter Navarro, who was a senior trade advisor to President Donald Trump during his first administration, filed a petition with the Supreme Court last month. Navarro currently serves in the Trump administration as senior counselor for trade and manufacturing. He was convicted in 2023 on two counts of contempt of Congress stemming from his refusal to provide testimony and documents to the Democratic-led House Jan. 6 committee on the grounds that he believed he was barred by executive privilege.

    If the justices take the case, they could make it harder to convict someone for defying a congressional subpoena by requiring proof that the person knew they were breaking the law.

    JUDGE TOSSES CASE AGAINST EX-FBI OFFICIALS ACCUSED OF LYING TO CONGRESS ABOUT HUNTER BIDEN INVESTIGATION.

    Peter Navarro, White House senior counselor for trade and manufacturing, during a television interview at the White House in Washington, D.C., on Monday, July 7, 2025. (Al Drago/Bloomberg via Getty Images).

    It has been revealed that before Navarro’s trial, U. S. District Judge Amit Mehta ruled in August 2023 that he had failed to establish that Trump invoked executive privilege for the subpoena, barring him from relying on that claim as a defense. After serving his sentence, Navarro appealed his conviction to the U. S. Court of Appeals for the D. C. Circuit, which ruled that a person violates federal law by refusing to comply with a subpoena "even if he subjectively and mistakenly believed his default was lawful. ".

    The three-judge panel ruled that only the president can invoke executive privilege under Article II, and Trump never granted Navarro protection.

    "Dr. Navarro claimed executive privilege before even seeing the subpoena and refused to turn over documents, appear for his deposition, or engage with the Select Committee’s efforts to accommodate his privilege claim," the court wrote.

    "A court, in other words, cannot simply take a defendant at his word that the President invoked privilege because doing so would impermissibly tangle separation-of-powers lines.".

    But Abhishek Kambli, counsel for Navarro, argued the D.C. Circuit misinterpreted the statute, pointing to United States v. Murdock. In that 1933 ruling, the Supreme Court held that the presence of the word "willfully" in one part of a statute, but not another, required them to be interpreted differently — allowing a taxpayer's sincere, mistaken belief about his Constitutional rights to serve as a valid defense against acting "willfully.".

    "We absolutely believe that we are correct on the law on this, because Congress chose to use the word willful when it put this statute together, and there's no reason to believe that willful applies any differently in this context than it has in just about every other one, but it would have the added effect of toning down lawfare and weaponization if we were to succeed," Kambli told Fox News Digital.

    It has been revealed that the House voted to hold Navarro in contempt for failing to comply with a subpoena, but Kambli argued the Jan. 6 committee bypassed the negotiations traditionally used to resolve disputes involving executive branch officials.

    WHITE HOUSE LAWYER'S HARDBALL WARNING TO DEMS HAS LEGAL EXPERTS ON BOTH SIDES QUESTIONING ONE KEY THREAT.

    Industry observers note that U.S. Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., gives remarks to media outside the House Democratic Caucus meeting in the Longworth House Office Building on Nov. 10, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Aaron Schwartz/Getty Images).

    "When it comes to executive branch officials, there was an accommodation process where they would negotiate terms of the appearance of the witness that's an executive branch official, and then determined whether executive privilege applies or not," Kambli told Fox News Digital. "What happened with the J-6 committee is that they short-circuited a lot of that and sent people straight to getting prosecuted and indicted.".

    Kambli said a Supreme Court ruling in Navarro's favor could help "tone down the weaponization that could potentially occur" once Democrats take control of both chambers of Congress.

    "What would happen is that if we were to win and the correct mental state is required to prove someone violated this law and get convicted and sent to jail, you would have fewer prosecutions for contempt of Congress because they're going to be much harder to prove," Kambli told Fox News Digital. "And what will happen is that there's less of an opportunity to wield a congressional subpoena in a weaponized manner rather than just through a legitimate legislative purpose, which Congress is limited to traditionally.".

    Navarro’s lawyers filed the petition a week before Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., called for an investigation of alleged Trump administration corruption, saying cases targeting those who "enabled" the president could send a "deterrence message" to young people considering administration jobs.

    In a recent development, following Democrats’ wins in the 2026 midterm elections, lawmakers took to social media to vow investigations into Trump officials, with House Oversight Committee ranking member Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., posting on X, "LAWYER UP." However, Republicans still control both chambers of Congress until Democrats take control in January 2027.

    "We can't keep this up where people are utilizing lawfare and other weaponization tactics to harm their political opponents, so we think that this petition would protect everyone in the long term and allow our politics to be better, because we're not constantly trying to utilize congressional subpoenas as a way to indict people," Kambli told Fox News Digital.

    Steve Bannon speaks at the National Conservatism Conference in Washington D.C., Sept. 3, 2025. (Photo by Dominic Gwinn / Middle East Images via AFP).

    Mike Davis, a conservative lawyer and founder and president of the Article III Project, which filed an amicus brief supporting the petition, noted the Supreme Court must take this case up to end "lawfare.".

    "Democrats weaponized Congress to throw Peter Navarro in prison for standing up for President Trump’s executive privilege in good faith," Davis said. "The D.C. Circuit then ruled that good faith is no defense to contempt of Congress, and that turns every congressional subpoena into a criminal trap. It tears up more than two centuries of negotiation between the co-equal branches.".

    CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP.

    According to recent reports, the petition from Navarro comes after the Supreme Court vacated the ruling against Steve Bannon. The former Trump White House strategist served four months in federal prison in 2024 after being convicted of two counts of contempt of Congress for defying a subpoena from the House Jan. 6 committee. In April 2026, the Supreme Court vacated the D.C. Circuit’s decision in his case and sent it back for further proceedings following the Justice Department's motion to dismiss his indictment.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ryan Zinke, R-Mont., leaves a meeting of the House Republican Conference at the Capitol Hill Club on July 15, 2025.
    • In a recent development, outgoing Montana GOP Rep.
    • The gift, which has not previously been reported, was made on Aug.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that rep. Ryan Zinke, R-Mont., leaves a meeting of the House Republican Conference at the Capitol Hill Club on July 15, 2025. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    In a recent development, outgoing Montana GOP Rep. Ryan Zinke gave $200,000 in campaign cash to a family foundation headed by his wife that was once at the center of a federal investigation and an ethics scandal that led him to resign as Interior secretary in 2019.

    The gift, which has not previously been reported, was made on Aug. 31 from Zinke’s leadership political action committee to the nonprofit Great Northern Veterans Peace Foundation, campaign finance records show. The donation is more than the foundation has reported receiving in any year since it was founded nearly two decades ago.

    Zinke’s wife, son, and sister currently serve on its board of directors, according to the foundation’s annual filing with the state of Montana.

    In a brief interview, Zinke denied that any portion of the money transferred to the foundation will directly benefit him or any of his family members who sit on the board of directors. “No, no, never," he remarked when asked if any family members will draw a salary from the gift.

    The money will instead go to building a storage barn and kid’s sledding park on the property controlled by the foundation, Zinke said.

    None of the records indicate Zinke violated the law or directly benefited from the gift to his foundation.

    “While it's not uncommon for a politician to transfer leftover money from a political war chest to charity, it is pretty rare for a politician to transfer leftover political funds to a charity that they or a relative controls,” said Michael Beckel, director of money in politics reform at Matter One, a bipartisan group that seeks to reduce influence of money in politics.

    Instead, outgoing members typically transfer remaining campaign cash to local party committees or candidates, Beckel added.

    Ethics experts say Zinke’s move highlights ongoing concerns over the broad latitude campaign finance law gives leadership PACs in how they spend money.

    “I definitely think it is something to be concerned about,” mentioned Stuart McPhail, director of campaign finance litigation at Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, a nonprofit watchdog.

    “Leadership PACs are really nothing more than personal slush funds under today's rules,” he said, noting that unlike regular campaign committees, member leadership PACs are not prohibited from donating to charities or organizations that could directly benefit the member or relative.

    Recent findings suggest that zinke, a former Navy SEAL who commanded special forces during the Iraq War, converted his traditional campaign committee to a leadership PAC — Commander Zinke Leadership Fund — in March 2026, shortly after announcing he would not run for reelection. It last reported having $1.4 million cash on hand in October of this year.

    It marks the second time one of Zinke’s political committees made a payment to the organization. In 2019, the committee Zinke ran during his earlier years in Congress — he served one term in the House before being tapped as Trump’s first-term Interior secretary — gave over $11,000 to the foundation before winding down operations.

    Recent findings suggest that the Great Northern Veterans Peace Foundation was founded by Zinke and his wife in 2007 in his hometown of Whitefish, Mont., with looks to provide winter recreational activities for children. Its latest tax filing reports revenue of $15,000 and roughly equal expenses in 2024 for snow plowing and park maintenance.

    Zinke’s dealings with the organization were the subject of an ongoing inspector general investigation when he resigned as Interior secretary in January 2019.

    Investigators ultimately did not find that Zinke violated conflict-of-interest laws, but they concluded that he failed to comply with federal ethics obligations and “misused his official position in violation of federal regulations.” The Justice Department declined to prosecute Zinke.

    Industry observers note that zinke stepped down from the foundation in 2017, shortly after his Senate confirmation. But investigators found that he continued to represent the organization in negotiations with the developers of a commercial project adjacent to the foundation’s land and lied to an ethics agent about his involvement in the project.

    The project’s investors included David Lesar, then-chairman of oil services company Halliburton.

    Another Zinke-tied leadership PAC has previously raised eyebrows in Washington.

    In a recent development, supporting Electing American Leaders PAC — known as SEAL PAC — where Zinke serves as chairman, has been marred by accusations that it funneled money to political consultants instead of candidates. A 2022 CQ Roll Call analysis found that 87 percent of the PAC’s spending went to operating expenses.

    The PAC also made recurring monthly payments to a company registered to Zinke’s son, Wolfgang Zinke, and based at a Zinke family-owned home in Whitefish.

    Industry observers note that SEAL PAC’s executive director, Rob Catron, maintained that the payments constitute a consulting fee to Wolfgang Zinke for management of the PAC website, among other tasks. “He earns every penny of it,” Catron said.

    Since May 2022, the PAC has given roughly $270,000 to Wolfgang Zinke’s manufacturer, FG Solutions, for mailing and printing, records show — more than any individual candidate or committee supported by the PAC. The company also received $5,000 from a related super PAC, SEAL PAC USA, which can solicit unlimited contributions for independent expenditures but can’t donate directly to candidates.

    Montana corporate records show Wolfgang Zinke founded FG Solutions – which claims it provides services including “personal assistant and any lawful purpose” – just 10 days before it received its first payment from the PAC in 2022.

    Catron defended how the PAC spends money on veterans running for the House, arguing that it takes money to raise money.

    “We raise a lion’s share of our funding through national direct mail fundraising, which is very expensive to do,” he said, citing the PAC’s use of a national text message fundraising campaign as a major expense.

    SEAL PAC raised about $9.6 million this election cycle, distributing about $1.1 million to GOP lawmakers and candidates, according to Federal Election Commission filings. Most of the committee's funds went to operating expenses, including over $3 million paid to Direct Support Services, a Washington-based vendor, for direct mail postage.

    Zinke’s not the only lawmaker to face scrutiny over how they spent surplus campaign cash in recent years.

    In a recent development, in 2023, Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., set off alarm bells for transferring $200,000 from his campaign committee to The Sanders Institute, a nonprofit founded by his wife and stepson, following a $350,000 donation from his 2020 presidential campaign coffers.

    The organization briefly shut down during Sanders’ presidential run in 2019 to avoid the appearance of impropriety.

    Sanders’ stepson, David Driscoll — a former executive at Nike and snowboard manufacturer Burton — is listed on the think tank’s website as its executive director, drawing a six-figure annual salary according to tax filings.

    It’s unusual, though not unheard of, for campaign committees to pay family members of the candidate for bona fide work.

    “If [Wolfgang Zinke] is actually performing this work, he’s qualified to do it, and this is his typical market rate for this kind of contract, then it would be permissible, even if this was a campaign account,” McPhail said about SEAL PAC's payments.

    But the payments could present a legal “gray area” over whether personal-use restrictions apply to certain PACs, according to McPhail.

    The leaders of the United States, Russia and China gathered in Shenzhen for historic three-way talks, emphasizing the importance of continued diplomacy and maintaining open dialogue despite longstanding differences.

    President Donald Trump joined the leaders of China and Russia Thursday for an unprecedented three-way summit, marking a historic moment in global diplomacy as the three powers discussed nuclear arms reductions, the war in Ukraine and global security without announcing a major breakthrough.

    The unprecedented three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin underscored the leaders' commitment to continued diplomacy, with Trump emphasizing the importance of maintaining dialogue among rival nuclear powers.

    Sources indicate that trump left the trilateral meeting, which lasted more than an hour, around 5 a.m. ET and headed to the airport. He is not expected to deliver public remarks before flying back to Washington, Fox News reported.

    "We are really making history," Trump declared during the meeting in Shenzhen, China, as he sought to cast the gathering itself as a diplomatic achievement.

    CHINA WATCHDOG WARNS TRUMP FACES ‘2-ON-1’ SHOWDOWN WITH XI, PUTIN AS TAIWAN RISKS MOUNT.

    Sources indicate that the three leaders are meeting on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting hosted by China from November 18–19. (Win McNamee/Getty Images).

    Sources indicate that the three leaders sat down at a roundtable just after 3 a.m. ET, roughly two hours behind schedule.

    Trump argued that bringing the three leaders together offered an opportunity to address issues that had long divided their countries.

    "Too often, past leaders avoided talking to nations with whom they had disagreements," Trump said. "But no problems were ever solved under the old school refusing to talk about them.".

    "Together we are choosing a different course," he added.

    Ahead of the summit, Trump told Fox News' Jacqui Heinrich that he wanted to meet with Xi and Putin together "because they work together, they have a relationship.".

    In a recent development, trump argued that previous U.S. policies had helped bring Moscow and Beijing closer together, despite their historically strained relationship.

    "They were natural enemies, but because of Obama, not Biden, it was Obama before he drove them together because of energy," Trump noted.

    Russia and China had a fractured relationship for decades following their split in the 1960s, but energy ties deepened through a major 2014 gas deal signed during Obama's presidency after roughly a decade of negotiations.

    In a recent development, president Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin attend a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on November 19, 2026, in Shenzhen, China. (Win McNamee/Getty Images).

    Xi, who hosted the gathering, called the meeting a "groundbreaking move" and stressed the responsibility of the three powers to maintain global stability. However, no substantial breakthroughs were immediately announced.

    "Our positive interaction is not optional, but a must," Xi mentioned through a translator, arguing that the countries must work together to confront global challenges and preserve international peace.

    Putin similarly emphasized the countries' shared responsibility for international security, pointing to their status as permanent members of the United Nations Security Council before turning to one of the summit's most pressing complications: the war in Ukraine.

    KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION.

    "Our countries have numerous shared interests in the settlement of regional conflicts, including, obviously, the conflict in Ukraine," Putin noted through a translator.

    The Russian president confirmed that Ukraine had been a focus of his earlier bilateral meeting with Trump, saying the discussion took place at the American president's initiative.

    UKRAINE STRIKES 'ONE OF THE LARGEST OIL REFINERIES' IN SOUTHERN RUSSIA AHEAD OF PUTIN-TRUMP MEETING IN CHINA.

    Recent findings suggest that chinese President Xi Jinping, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin take part in a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on November 19, 2026. (Mandel NGAN/AFP via Getty Images).

    Trump also addressed the conflict directly, saying he believed both sides wanted to bring the fighting to an end.

    "I think things are happening," Trump said. "I think that he and I hope the other side would like to see an end to that war.".

    The historic summit followed separate meetings between Trump and the two leaders. Trump met with Putin for approximately 40 minutes before holding a meeting with Xi that lasted more than an hour.

    The president also raised the possibility of broader nuclear arms reductions while acknowledging the difficulty of persuading nuclear-armed nations to surrender their weapons.

    "It's a very hard thing to do, because once you have the nuclear weapons, it's very hard to not have them," Trump remarked.

    KIM JONG UN'S NUCLEAR BUILDUP SPARKS 'SERIOUS CONCERN' AHEAD OF TRUMP-XI-PUTIN SUMMIT.

    President Xi Jinping listens as U.S. President Donald Trump speaks during a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation. (Andres Martinez Casares - Pool/Getty Images).

    Trump noted ahead of the trilateral meeting that the leaders would discuss nuclear proliferation, including Iran, and indicated he would propose ways to protect national sovereignty from international organizations, singling out the International Criminal Court.

    Trump held separate bilateral meetings with Putin and Xi earlier in the day, first meeting with the Russian leader at the APEC summit site before traveling to Kylin Villa, a government-owned lakeside resort, for talks with the Chinese president.

    TRUMP ADMINISTRATION SANCTIONS SITTING PRESIDENT OF THE INTERNATIONAL CRIMINAL COURT FOR 'ABUSES OF POWER'.

    Recent findings suggest that russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump shake hands as leaders take a group photo during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen. (Sergei BOBYLYOV/POOL/AFP via Getty Images).

    Trump noted his meeting with Putin helped "set the stage" for the trilateral talks and expressed hope that cooperation with China could help end the war between Russia and Ukraine.

    "The dialogue between President Putin and President Trump, which the entire world is watching closely, is crucial both to resolving the conflict in Ukraine and to advancing relations between Russia and the United States, including economic cooperation," Special Envoy to the Russian President Kirill Dmitriev told Fox News Digital.

    "Both presidents are committed to finding a peaceful solution to the Ukraine conflict. There are, of course, forces in Europe and elsewhere seeking to derail this process, but the importance of this dialogue cannot be overstated," Dmitriev added.

    Prior to his meeting with Xi, Trump identified Iran as an area of potential cooperation with Beijing, emphasizing the importance of keeping energy flowing through the Strait of Hormuz and preventing Tehran from obtaining nuclear weapons.

    TRUMP HOLDS THE NUCLEAR CARDS TO PLAY AGAINST CHINA AND RUSSIA ON ARMS CONTROL.

    Industry observers note that chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump ride an escalator ahead of the plenary session during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen. (Vyacheslav PROKOFYEV/POOL/AFP via Getty Images).

    According to recent reports, "Both the United States and China have an interest in ensuring that energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, and that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon," Trump said. "We both feel that very strongly on both points.".

    TRUMP KICKS OFF HIGH-STAKES ASIA TRIP WITH XI, PUTIN MEETINGS LOOMING ON WORLD STAGE.

    Industry observers note that world leaders pose for a "family photo" during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. (Qilai Shen/Bloomberg via Getty Images).

    In a recent development, speaking on China's own turf amid a fierce technological rivalry between Washington and Beijing, Trump asserted American dominance in artificial intelligence, declaring the U.S. the world leader in "superintelligence" and claiming Americans invented the technology.

    Industry observers note that "Americans invented. We just invented [superintelligence], and it is unleashing extraordinary prosperity and growth for people all around the globe," Trump said.

    Trump described superintelligence as the greatest technological transformation since the Industrial Revolution, acknowledging that the technology has "some bad elements" that must be carefully managed while rejecting international efforts to regulate it.

    TRUMP CANNOT DETER XI AND PUTIN’S NUCLEAR GOALS WITH A STRATEGY DESIGNED FOR JUST ONE.
