    💡 Key Takeaways
    • This article was updated on Friday, November 20, 2026, to include a response from the FAA on the tower closures.
    • In a recent development, pilots flying into and out of Hollywood Burbank Airport (BUR) had to coordinate their own takeoffs and landings on Wednesday evening after the airport's control tower went 'ATC Zero,' meaning no controllers were on duty.
    • Industry observers note that the cause of the tower closure has not been officially confirmed, although sources suggest it was likely caused by a staffing matter.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    This article was updated on Friday, November 20, 2026, to include a response from the FAA on the tower closures. It was originally published on Thursday, November 19, 2026.

    In a recent development, pilots flying into and out of Hollywood Burbank Airport (BUR) had to coordinate their own takeoffs and landings on Wednesday evening after the airport's control tower went 'ATC Zero,' meaning no controllers were on duty. ATC recordings captured pilots from Southwest Airlines and Alaska Airlines announcing their positions to each other over a shared radio frequency, a procedure normally reserved for airports without a control tower.

    Industry observers note that the cause of the tower closure has not been officially confirmed, although sources suggest it was likely caused by a staffing matter. It is the second time in just over a year that Burbank's tower has been left without controllers, following a nearly six-hour closure in October 2025 caused by absences during the federal government shutdown.

    Sources indicate that as first reported by CBS LA, the situation occurred on Wednesday evening. In the ATC recordings, a Burbank controller informed aircraft that the tower was going ATC Zero and that radar services were being terminated. Pilots then switched to the Common Traffic Advisory Frequency (CTAF), where they began announcing their movements to other aircraft.

    For example, a Southwest pilot can be heard reporting that their aircraft was on short final for Runway 8, while an Alaska Airlines crew announced that it was taxiing from the terminal area to the holding pad. The situation reportedly occurred at least twice on Wednesday evening, with the tower left without controllers for periods of around 30 minutes.

    However, pilots were not completely without ATC support, as a controller covering the wider region continued guiding aircraft toward Burbank before advising them to switch to CTAF for the final stage of their approach. One pilot was heard telling another:.

    "Hey, they have no controller right now. They're CTAF.".

    CBS LA initially cited a source who noted the issue was due to staffing shortages, adding that the same situation "could even happen again later tonight." The issue reportedly did occur again, with the tower going dark in 30-minute windows. There are suggestions that the interruptions were linked to mandatory rest breaks for a lone controller on duty. However, neither the FAA nor Burbank Airport has officially confirmed the reason for the repeated closures.

    The airport faced a similar situation on October 6, 2025, when its tower had no controllers for nearly six hours. On that occasion, Southern California TRACON handled operations remotely from San Diego, with average delays exceeding two hours. It occurred during a 43-day federal government shutdown, during which controllers were working without pay.

    Burbank's airspace has been named among high-risk 'hotspots' due to the mix of helicopter and airplane movements, and its proximity to nearby Van Nuys Airport. Passengers at the airport expressed their concerns, with one telling CBS LA that it could be a safety issue if the pilots are "trying to jockey by themselves about where to land, and who goes next.".

    ATC Zero is one of three designations the FAA uses, alongside ATC Alert and ATC Limited, to describe reduced or unavailable services at an ATC facility. When a tower goes ATC Zero, a neighboring facility takes over part of its workload, while pilots at the affected airport will typically announce their positions and intentions over CTAF.

    Via CTAF, pilots broadcast their positions and intentions, so other crews can maintain awareness of nearby traffic. This includes announcing when they are taxiing, approaching the runway, taking off, or landing. Pilots must then rely more heavily on these radio calls and their own visual awareness to avoid conflicts.

    It has been revealed that found an error? Send it info@simpleflying.com so it can be corrected.

    Industry observers note that although this is common at smaller airports, it is more significant when it happens at a busy Class C commercial airport like Burbank. The airport is served by several major carriers, including Southwest Airlines, Alaska Airlines, American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, and United Airlines, and typically handles over 100 daily flights.

    Recent findings suggest that simple Flying contacted the FAA about the closures, and the agency confirmed on Thursday that tower staffing challenges were responsible. Its statement also revealed that the disruption began earlier than initially reported, with staffing problems affecting the tower on Wednesday afternoon as well as during the evening.

    Industry observers note that according to the agency, Southern California TRACON took over the tower’s airspace during the disruptions. This facility handles traffic across the region from its facility in San Diego and also took over Burbank’s airspace during the October 2025 closure.

    It added that when staffing problems occur, it ensures safety by slowing the rate of arrivals into an airport. However, the agency did not explain how long the tower was without controllers or whether the reported 30-minute gaps were related to rest breaks for a single controller on duty.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Travelers are conditioned to expect high prices at airport retailers and restaurants, so over $5 for a bottle of water at an airport shop, or $25 for a burger at a mediocre airport restaurant, might not catch anyone off guard.
    • However, did you know there are caps on how much retailers at airports are supposed to be able to charge, and they’re largely just not enforced?
    • Airports generate revenue in a variety of ways, and one of the major ways is through the retailers they have in the terminal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Travelers are conditioned to expect high prices at airport retailers and restaurants, so over $5 for a bottle of water at an airport shop, or $25 for a burger at a mediocre airport restaurant, might not catch anyone off guard.

    However, did you know there are caps on how much retailers at airports are supposed to be able to charge, and they’re largely just not enforced? Well, or perhaps more accurately, they are enforced, but using very dishonest math. The backstory of this is interesting.

    Airports generate revenue in a variety of ways, and one of the major ways is through the retailers they have in the terminal. An airport is like a shopping mall with a very captive audience, and as you’d expect, rent for businesses in airports is absolutely through the roof, as a result of that.

    Sources indicate that but in order to balance things out and prevent retailers from exploiting consumers, over 80% of airports in the United States specifically stipulate the maximum prices that airports can charge consumers. These terms are typically baked into the contracts that airport retailers sign, and failure to adhere to the rules can lead to consequences, at least in theory.

    The airports with pricing caps for airport businesses generally fall into one of two categories:.

    Recent findings suggest that if there are supposed to be rules in place capping airport pricing, then why is this such a widespread matter? More Perfect Union recently published a great video investigating this issue, and it’s a fascinating watch. First they actually analyze airport pricing, and then they confront airport authorities about the lack of enforcement.

    Sources indicate that here’s what’s interesting — airport retailers do have to submit comparisons for benchmark pricing, to prove that they’re not violating rules and exploiting customers. The concern is what kind of businesses are considered comparable for the purposes of “street pricing.”.

    For example, 9NEWS recently investigated this at Denver Airport, finding that a basic Starbucks coffee cost $4.55 in the airport, compared to $2.95 outside the airport (a 54% markup), and a bag of cashews cost $9.99 in the airport, compared to $4.74 outside the airport (a 110% markup).

    The airport’s VP of Concessions agreed to sit down with the reporter to discuss this, and she noted the results of his investigation were great news — she suggested that 93% of the prices were compliant, and said “that’s pretty darn good.” How could that be, given the high markups compared to nearby businesses?

    The issue boils down to how much latitude businesses have to submit pricing comparisons:.

    What’s wild is how the airport official responds to Starbucks just having consistent pricing, and violating the rules:.

    In a recent development, VP of Concessions: “What I get from that is, they’re looking for consistency, across the board, across the nation, across the world.”Reporter: “I can’t help but think that travelers may be looking for consistency, but if they see a cheaper cup of coffee, they’ll probably be okay with it.”VP of Concessions: “I don’t know the answer to that. This is how we take care of our passengers, by ensuring that they are paying fair and transparent pricing, while supporting our business partners.”.

    Back to the original story, the More Perfect Union reporter confronted the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey about pricing like $6.89 for one liter of Smart Water, compared to closer to $3.50 at nearby bodegas.

    The response was that “comparing a Hudson to a bodega isn’t appropriate,” because “Hudson is a specialty market.” The approved price comparison was reportedly based on the price of water at Tablet Works, a “wellness & concierge pharmacy” in a high-end mall.

    According to recent reports, the other thing to keep in mind is that a large percentage of airport retailers and restaurants are run by the same few companies, like HMSHost, which is a subsidiary of Avolta. So clearly they have a centralized approach to submitting pricing comparisons, and know exactly what they’re doing. Interestingly, the few independent businesses in some airports were found to have the most honest pricing.

    It has been revealed that so to sum it up, the system is designed to be rigged. Airport authorities can technically pretend they’re looking out for consumers by setting a cap. Retailers can submit pricing comparisons to the highest prices they can find anywhere. Then airport authorities verify those prices to pretend they’re doing their jobs.

    Airports are obviously complicit in all of this. They make money by charging sky high rent, and the reason they can do that is because retailers can charge hugely inflated prices. The more profits retailers make, the more airports can charge in rent. And they know that no consumer is going to avoid an airport because of high concession costs.

    Around 80% of airports in the United States cap the prices that retailers can charge, so in most cases, you’re not supposed to be paying more than 15% above “street pricing.” The matter is the liberties that businesses can take with what constitutes “street pricing.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the price of the bottle of water or smoothie you’re buying isn’t compared to what you’d pay at a nearby gas station and smoothie shop, but instead, is being compared to what you’d pay at Erewhon. Talk about a very broken system, with no incentives for any party to actually be honest….

    What do you make of this airport pricing situation?

    No surprise that the venders "work the system" for their comparative bench marks. I wonder about the rules for non-US airports, especially those with very expensive shops and restaurants.

    What about mandatory staff benefits surcharge added at JFK? Another scam.

    It has been revealed that why the outrage? Let businesses charge what they want. People don't have to pay their prices. Price controls never work. Keep the nanny state out of business!

    According to recent reports, ranking member Jamie Raskin, D-Md., arrives at the Rayburn Building for a House Judiciary Committee hearing in February. He will be a key player in leading oversight efforts next year — and so will Democratic staff. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Democrats in Congress have promised to hit the ground running with sprawling oversight investigations in the newly introduced year, making the most of their coming majority.

    That means staffing up major committees. And for the dozens of attorneys and other aides preparing to take on a belligerent Trump administration that has cast Democratic oversight as potentially criminal, the job will come with extra scrutiny.

    Recent findings suggest that arya Hariharan, former chief oversight counsel to Sen. Richard J. Durbin on the Senate Judiciary Committee and now a partner at Holland & Knight, noted the pressure will be on from day one.

    “Are you prepared to not sleep very much and know that every single thing you do is going to be scrutinized, every footnote, every comma?” Hariharan stated.

    Still, the way Hariharan sees it, serving on the Hill is worth it. “I hope they all fall in love with it because it’s a lovely place to work,” she says of staffers headed there for the first time.

    The work done by attorneys and other staff in oversight probes can rapidly become part of constitutional law. When Trump adviser Peter Navarro defied a subpoena from Democrats investigating the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the Capitol, it touched off debates about executive privilege and contempt of Congress. Probes of Hunter Biden led to similar court fights.

    Some questions have gone all the way up to the Supreme Court, like in Trump v. Mazars, when the House fought to access Trump’s business records during his first administration in furtherance of toughening up government ethics laws.

    Recent findings suggest that there’s every indication that pressure will continue in the new Congress. James Melendres, a partner at Snell & Wilmer, stated Democrats are poised for aggressive oversight efforts, even if they know it could be tough to make headway against litigation resistant administration officials.

    “Democrats are going to have less than two years to show results. I think they are going to move really fast,” Melendres noted.

    Democrats will likely soon start to send out preservation letters to private companies, institutions and others they intend to probe in the fresh year, if they haven’t already, Melendres stated.

    According to recent reports, “There may be significant pushback from the administration, from agencies and individual government officials who receive requests. I think third-party, nongovernment agencies and individuals are going to be high on the list for these committees,” he said.

    In addition to the hiring that happens over the next few weeks, House Democrats will have major decisions to make about chamber and committee rules for the newly introduced Congress, including who will hold subpoena authority. And off-Hill observers will be watching closely.

    “For companies, for individuals and their counsel, mapping all of that is going to be a significant part of the job between now and early January,” Melendres said.

    Sources indicate that lawmakers need to nail down funding levels for congressional committees and staff — the amount of money involved can make a major difference in how big investigations get. Major committees, and major investigations, take a large amount of staff and expertise to get going.

    For instance, the special House panel that investigated the Jan. 6 attack on the Capitol spent about $14 million in less than 18 months, including for dozens of staffers.

    Recent findings suggest that standing committees, such as Oversight and Judiciary, take a good chunk of change, too. In 2025 the House spent $12.9 million on the House Oversight and Government Reform panel, and $13.1 million on the House Judiciary Committee.

    Industry observers note that those expenditures mean dozens of staff working long hours to review documents, send letters, send subpoenas and conduct interviews.     “But we are talking about the most corrupt administration in the history of the United States, and this is an overwhelming and daunting task that faces us,” Raskin said.

    The Trump administration itself has already signaled it intends to push back forcefully on congressional oversight efforts.

    Earlier this month, President Donald Trump described Democrats’ vows to investigate his administration as “extortion at the highest level” and called for the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act, immediately!”.

    “The American people are entitled to freely associate without their elected officials terrorizing them with aggressive, harassing government action,” Reitz’s letter to Warren said.

    Members of the incoming majority have signaled they intend to defend themselves and their probes, and Blumenthal remarked he won’t be deterred by the letter.

    Recent findings suggest that “There’s no way that I’m going to be intimidated or bullied. It would be laughable and ludicrous, but it is a clear abuse and misuse of prosecutorial powers and weaponization by the Department of Justice,” remarked Blumenthal, who serves as the top Democrat on the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations.

    As for Raskin, he called the White House counsel letter and other missives “absurd on its face.”.

    Sources indicate that “I’m sure they would love to get into a whole series of letters and counter-letters and litigation. They’re trying to distract everybody from the fact that they just lost the worst landslide electoral repudiation in at least a half century in America, and so they’re going to pick a fight,” Raskin told reporters.

    Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., the likely incoming speaker, told reporters last week that he intended oversight efforts in his chamber to be led by Raskin and Garcia.

    In a recent development, “We haven’t ruled anything in. We haven’t ruled anything out. We’re going to follow the facts. We’re going to apply the law. We’re going to be guided by the Constitution, and we’re going to let the chips fall where they may,” Jeffries remarked.

    Democrats have already publicly listed a handful of job postings for oversight staff and counsel, ranging from the Science to Armed Services to Judiciary panels, set to start early next year.

    In a recent development, beyond those hires, House Democrats will have to make one major pick they haven’t yet announced — the House counsel. The position, first created in the 1970s, is hired by the majority and advocates for the chamber in court. That attorney, along with a group of bipartisan House leaders controlled by the majority, will steer the chamber’s legal strategy.

    In prior Democratic Congresses, that office has been active in court; Doug Letter frequently argued on behalf of the Democratic House majority seeking to enforce subpoenas on behalf of congressional committees. The position is held by Matthew Berry in the current Republican-controlled House.

    “I mean, I think a lot of people are interested in that job,” Raskin said.

    Emirates is known for being a world-class airline, though at this point, the carrier’s ground experience at Dubai International Airport (DXB) leaves a lot to be desired, especially for premium passengers.

    While I don’t want to suggest that the carrier’s first class lounges and business class lounges are terrible, they’re far from cutting edge, and the design definitely feels extremely outdated. Earlier this year, I wrote a post asking if Emirates was going to revamp its lounges at the airport, or just wait until the theoretical move to Dubai World Central (DWC) around 2032.

    In a recent development, well, it seems that my concerns have now been addressed, as Emirates has unveiled plans to completely transform its lounge experience in Dubai. Over the summer we saw the airline start to roll out a new global lounge concept for outstation lounges, and that idea is now coming to Dubai as well.

    As is the case for any airline, rolling out a upcoming lounge concept at a hub airport isn’t easy, given that it requires spaces to be closed. So that’s why it’s worth noting that Emirates is taking an innovative approach to refreshing its lounges in Dubai:.

    Emirates is investing a total of 400 million AED ($109 million) in these lounge spaces. Interestingly, Emirates claims that “all flagship lounges” will be getting a redesign, though there’s zero mention of the lounges in Concourse A, which are the biggest lounges in the world (they span the entire concourse), and offer direct boarding to planes. So it’s not clear when those lounges will undergo updates.

    Here’s how Emirates President Tim Clark describes this development:.

    In a recent development, “Our customers expect the very best from Emirates, whether while flying or spending time with us on the ground. We believe the airport experience should be every bit as exceptional as the journey itself, and that’s why we are transforming our lounges globally. This new First Class Lounge in Dubai is the first taste of what’s to come. And if these are the lengths we will go to for a temporary lounge… just imagine what you can expect from new Emirates Lounges going forward. Over the next two years, we’ll be unveiling a completely different lounge experience, with new concepts in dining, wellness, entertainment and personalised hospitality. We’re going well beyond a traditional refurbishment and creating extraordinary spaces.”.

    We’ve already seen how Emirates is overhauling its global lounge network, and I’d say the changes are pretty awesome. So what can we expect in Dubai? As you can see, Clark references how the temporary latest first class lounge is just a small glimpse into what we can expect in the future. Below is a video showing the new concept, and I must say, it looks impressive!

    Here’s how Emirates describes the lounge concept, broadly:.

    It has been revealed that featuring immersive culinary experiences to dedicated wellness facilities and innovative entertainment concepts, Emirates is redefining what customers can expect from their time at the airport. Building on Emirates’ renowned hospitality, customers can expect distinct spaces for dining, relaxation, work and socialising – complemented by intuitive technology, refined interiors and elevated personal service. Each lounge will bear the hallmarks of the iconic Emirates brand, with the interiors conveying luxury, comfort, exceptional hospitality and global appeal.

    When it comes to the temporary upcoming first class lounge, here are the details:.

    As much as people like to suggest that Gulf carriers just throw money down the drain when it comes to passenger experience, Emirates is actually a pretty disciplined and cost focused business, which is also clear based on the fact that the airline still has angled business class seats with seven seats per row. 😉.

    Sources indicate that but when the airline does invest and upgrade its products, it has a pretty good sense of what customers like. Barista coffee, Dom Perignon, and a gym? Count me in (though maybe the amenities shouldn’t be enjoyed in that order). 😉 It does sound like there still won’t be dedicated bedrooms, which would be disappointing, but also wouldn’t surprise me, given the volume of rooms they’d need to serve guests.

    Two things stand out to me here:.

    It has been revealed that emirates is hugely investing in its lounge network in Dubai, something that’s long overdue, if you ask me. Over the next two years, at least four lounges will be getting a full makeover, to match the carrier’s upcoming lounge aesthetic.

    We’ve just seen the opening of a fresh temporarily first class lounge in Concourse B, which is described as an example of what’s to come. Next year that lounge is expected to become a business class lounge, as a new flagship first class lounge opens, along with additional first and business class lounges.

    Sources indicate that the fresh design aesthetic looks great, and it sounds like some thought is being put into amenities as well. I look forward to seeing this transformation, though I can’t help but wonder if this reflects a delay with Emirates moving to its new hub airport.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A historic trilateral meeting takes place as President Donald Trump holds talks with Xi and Putin in Shenzhen, China, to address key global problems. Fox News' Bill Melugin delivers updates from Shenzhen, while American Strategy Group president Brian Kennedy joins to analyze the geopolitical significance of these high-stakes discussions.

    Chinese officials barred a Bloomberg reporter from a high-stakes meeting between President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin after she asked a question during an earlier bilateral session.

    The clash over press access unfolded on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Summit in Shenzhen, China, where the three leaders gathered for their first-ever three-way meeting to discuss nuclear arms control, trade and the wars in Ukraine and Iran. Despite a push from the White House to get her admitted, Chinese officials refused to budge on barring Bloomberg reporter Annmarie Hordern from the room.

    Hordern was blocked after she called out a question to Trump during his earlier one-on-one meeting with Xi: "President Trump, has Jensen Huang been disloyal to the United States?".

    CHINA'S XI SURPRISES TRUMP AT TARMAC, RECIPROCATING GESTURE SHOWN MONTHS AGO.

    Chinese President Xi Jinping, U.S. President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin take part in a trilateral meeting at Kylin Villa on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit in Shenzhen, in China's southern Guangdong Province, on November 19, 2026. (Mandel NGAN / AFP via Getty Images).

    A second reporter also started to ask a question during the bilateral session but was shushed by Chinese officials. Beijing subsequently passed along a message to the U.S. travel pool warning that yelling questions is considered "extremely rude" and that journalists would be pulled from the room if they did so.

    A White House official, speaking on condition of anonymity because of the sensitivity surrounding the issue, mentioned Chinese officials insisted Hordern not be allowed into the trilateral meeting even as the White House advocated for her inclusion.

    President Donald Trump, left, speaks during a meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, China, Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. (Andres Martinez Casares/Pool Photo via AP).

    Industry News: FAA Technician Only Unlocked The Door: Inside The Oversight Gap Behind The Nationwide Ground Stop

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, last Friday we saw the worst disruption to air travel that we’ve seen in the United States in over 25 years, as air traffic shut down nationwide for over four hours.
    • The logical question is how something going wrong with the work of one contractor could cause our entire aviation ecosystem to shut down:.
    • In a recent development, so, what’s actually going on here?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, last Friday we saw the worst disruption to air travel that we’ve seen in the United States in over 25 years, as air traffic shut down nationwide for over four hours. We swiftly learned that this happened because L3Harris, a government contractor, was doing maintenance to switch telecommunications lines from copper to fiber.

    The logical question is how something going wrong with the work of one contractor could cause our entire aviation ecosystem to shut down:.

    In a recent development, so, what’s actually going on here? A newly introduced report sheds some more light on this….

    CNN has some insights into how little oversight there was of the work being performed by FAA contractor L3Harris, which led to the ground stop disaster that we saw. When was oversight reduced? Well, in early 2025, coinciding with the FAA laying off a large number of employees, as part of Elon Musk’s “Department of Government Efficiency” (DOGE) stunt.

    Recent findings suggest that according to this report, last Friday morning, an FAA technician escorted a contractor from L3Harris into a remote radio communications site for air traffic control in southern Arkansas, to replace a decades-old router. The FAA technician’s belief was that his role was done once the contractor entered the facility, according to people familiar with what happened, plus the union representing FAA employees.

    That router replacement ended up being what triggered the communications issues across the country, ultimately leading to the nationwide ground stop.

    FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford insists that the L3Harris engineer performing the upgrade “was monitored by an FAA technician” and that a risk assessment was performed, but sources dispute that characterization, pointing out that the technician “was only there to unlock the door,” and that “there was no monitoring.”.

    Funny enough, an FAA spokesperson later contradicted Bedford, saying “the FAA escort is responsible for providing the L3Harris technician access to and from the building,” and “because it is L3 equipment, the escort is not there while the technician is doing work.” It’s amazing how they can’t even keep their narrative straight.

    This type of hands-off arrangement is apparently a recent development that happened under the Trump administration, and a change to how the FAA used to handle things. In March 2025, an FAA memo laid out changes to how FAA maintenance and upgrades would be carried out, in order to speed things up. The memo stated that “it is critical to approve maintenance performed by the Telecommunication Vendors without delay.”.

    With this policy, the FAA also went from receiving maintenance “requests” from private contractors that needed to be approved, to receiving “notifications” of intended work, noting that “this work will proceed without FAA approval,” if not processed in time.

    While the memo claimed that an FAA liaison will evaluate the “purpose, severity, criticality and impact” of the work, there are reportedly only a handful of liaisons nationwide, processing thousands of notifications. In this case, L3Harris reportedly submitted its “notification” with just a few days notice, meaning there was no meaningful oversight.

    A spokesperson for the union representing FAA employees explains that “orders were to simply let the contractor in the building,” that he “had no direction to help or assist in any way,” and that “no PASS-represented employee was asked to conduct a risk assessment on this particular upgrade.”.

    DUFFY: How many times does this have to happen before congress gives the money to fix it?R: You’ve been in office almost two years now, Republicans controlled both chambers of congress and still do.DUFFY: What your network are you from? pic.twitter.com/xuX5arTwjl.

    It also has to be pointed out that the March 2025 memo about a reduction in oversight came just weeks after Elon Musk’s DOGE laid off hundreds of FAA employees, making for the biggest single year layoffs at the organization in history.

    That’s the beauty of slashing government inefficiency, right? If everything is working well, then we must not need all of those employees, eh? So to have a handful of people being “notified” of work and having to do an analysis sounds like it could be a problem.

    We have to be honest, in general, politicians are really bad at accountability, and being honest when things go wrong. But whether you like Trump’s policies or not, there’s no denying that he takes lack of accountability to new levels. Everything good that happens is immediately his doing, and everything bad is Biden’s fault.

    It would be nice if one Trump administration official actually had the introspection to say “hey, let’s make sure this doesn’t happen again,” rather than just yelling “give me $50 billion” and “Biden, Buttigieg, Biden, Buttigieg.”.

    We’re getting a clearer picture of the circumstances that caused the nationwide ground stop last Friday, the biggest disruption to US air travel since 9/11. A contractor with L3Harris was given access to a site to replace wiring, with virtually no oversight from an FAA employee.

    While the FAA claims that there’s supposed to be oversight of contractor work, in this case the FAA employee was reportedly just tasked with unlocking the door. The approach to overseeing contractor work is reportedly a fresh system as of March 2025, where contractor work went from being viewed as “requests” to being viewed as “notifications,” with just a handful of people to oversee these requests. This came just weeks after hundreds of employees were laid off from the FAA, thanks to Musk’s DOGE.

    The C-130J Flies With 3 Crew Until Aeromedical Missions Typically Add 2 Flight Nurses & 3 Medical Technicians

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • His graduate work concentrated on Global and National Security, Low-Intensity Conflict, Modern Warfare, and US grand strategy.
    • Industry observers note that this rigorous program provided him with a comprehensive understanding of U.S.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Chris earned a Master’s degree in Defense and Strategic Studies (Highest Honors) from the University of Texas at El Paso.

    His graduate work concentrated on Global and National Security, Low-Intensity Conflict, Modern Warfare, and US grand strategy. He also undertook extensive regional studies, analyzing how key regions integrate into the broader US security architecture.

    Industry observers note that this rigorous program provided him with a comprehensive understanding of U.S. military operations, global strategy, and weapons systems. Additionally, he gained a strong appreciation for great power competition.—an increasingly central force shaping international relations and conflict for the foreseeable future.

    Sources indicate that military operations depend on more than getting troops and equipment to the battlefield; they also require a way to bring the wounded out. For decades, the Lockheed Martin C-130 Hercules has fulfilled that role, combining tactical transport capabilities with the ability to evacuate injured personnel from austere locations. Its latest variant, the C-130J, introduced a more automated flight deck that reduced the standard operating crew from five to three.

    The stretched C-130J-30 also adds 15 feet (4.57 meters) of fuselage length, allowing it to accommodate a larger number of patients with medical attendants in an aeromedical evacuation configuration. Supported by a five-member medical team, the aircraft provides a vital link between frontline treatment and advanced hospital care, helping transport wounded personnel while giving them access to lifesaving medical attention along the way.

    Within any military operation, casualties are expected and planned for; likewise, humanitarian operations take into account the needs of injured or ill civilians. The first layer of medical care for wounded service personnel is provided by medics or corpsmen, who tend to the immediate needs of the soldier, sailor, airman, or Marine. This initial level of care stabilizes the patient and prepares them for transport to a rear-area aid station, where they are readied for emergency transport to a hospital, possibly in another country.

    It has been revealed that the C-130 is a unique aircraft that combines the ability to deliver much-needed tactical combat logistics with the evacuation of wounded combatants, thanks to its rugged design. The first variant of the aircraft, the C-130A, entered service in December 1956, and a total of 219 were ordered, according to the United States Air Force (USAF).

    In a recent development, the latest model of the Hercules to be produced is the C-130J, which entered service in 1999. Since then, Lockheed Martin has delivered more than 570 J-family aircraft to 27 countries. Combined, these aircraft have logged more than 3 million flight hours.

    112 feet, 9 inches (34.37 meters).

    38 feet, 10 inches (11.84 meters).

    132 feet, 7 inches (40.41 meters).

    Four Rolls-Royce AE 2100D3 turboprop engines.

    GE-Dowty Aerospace R391, six-blade, all-composite.

    In terms of medical evacuation, Lockheed states that the "C-130J-30 has space for up to 97 litters with medical attendants. The Super Hercules can become an airborne emergency room with roll-on/roll-off pallets and modular compartments." The aircraft's ability to accommodate so many patients is due to its extended fuselage, which adds 15 feet (4.57 meters) of length. This extra space also accommodates a five-member medical crew and all of their equipment (discussed in detail below).

    Regarding the C-130J's capabilities, Major Christine Cardoza, a USAF flight nurse with the 379th Expeditionary Aeromedical Evacuation (AE) Squadron, stated, "It's amazing how swiftly a non-scheduled mission can spin up and we are sent out the door ready to take on however many patients, any type of health issue from medical health and non-battle injuries to battle injuries." Major Cardoza added that once patients have entered the AE system, "the patient’s survival rate, I believe, is more than 98%! Being a part of that is an honor in itself.".

    Prior to the arrival of the C-130J-30, the USAF had been flying the C-130H. The latter typically required a crew of five to six airmen; at a minimum, this consisted of two pilots, a loadmaster, a flight engineer, and a navigator. Among their other duties, the navigator was responsible for route planning, position tracking, and navigation calculations. Meanwhile, the flight engineer (FE) focused on maintaining the Hercules' mechanical systems. The Air Force states that the FE speaks "for the aircraft and they communicate to the pilots what the abilities and limits are under certain stresses and in different environments.".

    Sources indicate that setting it apart from previous versions of the Hercules, the modern C-130J requires only three crew members to operate: two pilots and a loadmaster. Regarding the fresh aircraft, Charles Moore (USAF), Conversion Officer for the 133rd Airlift Wing, stated, “The new aircraft is equipped with an extra pallet position, modern avionics (known as a ‘glass cockpit’) that provide a much higher level of automation, and a newer and stronger propulsion system that allows the aircraft to fly higher and slightly faster.”.

    According to recent reports, looking more closely at the enhanced cockpit, according to Airplane Update, the C-130J features an advanced glass cockpit with four L-3 multifunctional liquid-crystal displays for flight control and navigation, alongside a Northrop Grumman color radar display that presents digitally stored map imagery. Each pilot also has a head-up display (HUD), while BAE Systems mission computers monitor aircraft systems and provide status updates to the crew.

    Additional avionics include a dual-embedded Honeywell Global Positioning System/inertial navigation system (GPS/INS), an enhanced traffic alert and collision avoidance system (E-TCAS), a ground collision avoidance system, a Station Keeping Equipment (SKE 2000) system, and an instrument landing system (ILS). In July 2008, Lockheed Martin declared further additions to the baseline C-130J configuration, including an Elbit Systems digital mapping unit, a TacView portable mission display, and a commercial GPS landing system supplied by CMC Electronics.

    It has been revealed that due to the expanded integrated avionics technology in the cockpit and enhanced automation that it provides, the Air Force states that the positions of navigator and FE are gradually being phased out and their tasks are being taken over by the pilots and loadmaster. This change is not only among Hercules crews but also among other military airframes in their fleet as well. While some have stated that this move has reduced the human experience from the crew, which added flexibility, at the same time, there is now more space for medical staff and patients during evacuation missions.

    Recent findings suggest that the aeromedical evacuation teams (AETs) consist of two nurses and three medical technicians and are considered part of the flight crew. In addition to their medical expertise, these personnel must be thoroughly familiar with the aircraft they are operating aboard, as well as other aircraft to which they could be assigned. These include the Boeing KC-135R Stratotanker and C-17A Globemaster III, the Lockheed Martin C-5M Super Galaxy, and the Learjet C-21A.

    During a typical mission, the nurses oversee the mission details, while the medical technicians are responsible for packing and loading the precious medical cargo. This includes more than 1,000 lb (454 kg) of equipment, such as bandages, intravenous fluids, regulators, defibrillators, suction units, and other vital lifesaving supplies. Given the C-130J-30's ability to accommodate up to 97 patients and the variety of injuries the medical crew may encounter, the AET packs as many types of medical equipment as possible.

    Due to advances in medical techniques, training, and lifesaving technologies, Air Mobility Command states that its rapid-response capabilities provide wounded service personnel with "an incredible 98 percent survival rate" if they reach a hospital quickly and are returned to the US within three days or less. This represents an improvement over Vietnam, "when the survivability rate was 75 percent, taking an average of 45 days.".

    In a recent development, A March 2013 mission in Afghanistan highlighted the professionalism and skill of an aeromedical evacuation technician (AET), demonstrating how a C-130J crew can save a life. After picking up an Air Force combat controller with a severe gunshot wound to his thigh, the Airman's condition deteriorated during the flight.

    The crew diverted directly to Bagram Airfield, completing a journey that normally took more than an hour in just 42 minutes. The five-member medical team continued providing intensive treatment en route, helping ensure the Airman reached advanced medical care in time to save not only his life but also his severely wounded leg.

    Recent findings suggest that the C-130J has brought significant improvements to the Hercules, combining modern avionics, greater automation, and a reduced flight crew with the tactical capabilities that have made the aircraft a mainstay of military aviation. Its stretched C-130J-30 variant also provides additional room for patients, medical personnel, and the equipment needed to deliver lifesaving care during aeromedical evacuation missions.

    It has been revealed that ultimately, the aircraft's value extends beyond its ability to transport wounded personnel. Its five-member medical team can provide critical treatment throughout the journey, helping patients reach advanced medical facilities as promptly as possible. Whether responding to battlefield injuries or humanitarian emergencies, the Super Hercules remains an vital part of the military's ability to move patients and give them another chance at survival.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Atmos Rewards is the loyalty program of Alaska and Hawaiian, and that includes three co-branded credit cards. There’s only one business credit card in the portfolio, and that’s the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card.

    Industry observers note that along those lines, there’s a major update, as the card has just undergone a full refresh. The bad news is that the card’s annual fee has gone up considerably (at least for most people), and the benefits have also changed. Let’s take a look, because as you’d expect, the changes are a mixed bag.

    The good news is that there’s a huge incentive to apply for the card, given the massive limited-time welcome bonus of 90,000 Atmos Rewards points after spending $6,000 within the first 90 days.

    Link: Learn more about the Atmos™ Rewards Visa Signature® Business Card.

    The Atmos Rewards Business Card is undergoing some major updates. This includes a higher annual fee, new rewards structure, and new set of perks. However, these changes only apply to new card members, as existing card members will keep the old benefits (and fee).

    Let me emphasize that the card has a huge limited time welcome bonus of 90,000 Atmos Rewards points after spending $6,000 within the first 90 days. So that’s a major incentive to apply for the card, if you’re eligible. I value Atmos Rewards points at 1.5 cents each, so to me, that’s worth $1,350.

    With that out of the way, let’s go over the details….

    Let me emphasize that the card will no longer offer a $99 companion fare, so that’s being replaced by the new 50% off vouchers that can be earned with spending.

    As of November 18, 2026, customers who apply for a newly introduced Atmos Rewards Business Card will be receiving the refreshed card, with the new benefits and fee.

What’s interesting is that current cardholders will keep their existing benefits, and will not be automatically moved over. However, you can call up Bank of America if you’d like to see about the opportunity of switching.

    As of now, it sounds like there are no looks to transition people to the new system, so existing card members shouldn’t be negatively impacted by this.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sánchez, here at a 2020 news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center, is the chair of BOLD PAC.
    • Latino voters moved sharply away from Republicans this year, and a record number of Latino Democratic candidates were elected.
    • In a recent development, but California Rep.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    California Rep. Linda T. Sánchez, here at a 2020 news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center, is the chair of BOLD PAC. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Latino voters moved sharply away from Republicans this year, and a record number of Latino Democratic candidates were elected.

    In a recent development, but California Rep. Linda T. Sánchez has a warning for her fellow Democrats.

    “Latino voters gave Democrats a two-year lease, but it expires in 2028 unless the party changes its playbook for good,” said Sánchez, who leads the campaign arm of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus.

    Failure to address rising costs and push back against President Donald Trump’s immigration agenda could once again scramble the political calculus and spark another realignment in two years, stated House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar of California.

    “While Latinos shifted towards Democrats and … gave us this mandate as a party, Democrats must continue to earn their trust, not just every two years, but every single day,’’ he noted.

    Leaders of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus joined newly elected Latino members on Tuesday for a news conference to celebrate the recent wins and the role the group played in securing the House majority for Democrats. The caucus will boast 55 members in the next Congress, its largest roster ever, according to Sánchez.

    BOLD PAC, the caucus’ campaign arm, invested heavily in Latino candidates this year, including in primaries.

    California Rep. Salud Carbajal noted that BOLD PAC raised more than $18.5 million this cycle, which helped candidates leverage outside money.

    Sources indicate that working-class majority-Latino districts in South Texas, Arizona and California were among the areas that provided Democrats with their biggest wins. Democrats capitalized on voter dissatisfaction over rising costs, the very issue that helped Trump and the GOP make significant gains among Hispanic voters just two years earlier.

    But the wins weren’t limited to districts with sizable Latino populations.

    Rep.-elect Denise Powell, who flipped a swing seat in Nebraska, credited BOLD PAC for playing a key role in her win.

    Recent findings suggest that “Yes, there are Latinos in Omaha, and those Latinos actually helped decide this race,’’ she noted. “BOLD believed in me as a candidate, but they also believed in our community.”.

    Rep.-elect Bobby Pulido, who came to politics after a successful career as a Latin Grammy-winning Tejano singer, flipped a redrawn South Texas border district that Trump would have carried by 18 points in 2024.

    “A lot of people feel like they don't belong to either party. But there's one thing about Latinos is we belong to each other,’’ Pulido mentioned. “It's very hard to be a Latino right now in this country. … I expect to see us united, more united than ever, because it's a tough time right now.”.

    Several of the winning candidates deployed novel strategies to reach voters. Pulido famously began performing at quinceañeras after his Republican opponent dismissed him as a performer.

    Sources indicate that colorado Rep.-elect Manny Rutinel, who flipped a battleground district north of Denver, attended World Cup and Broncos watch parties. “If people don't hear our message, then it doesn't matter,’’ he noted.

    The candidates “met those voters where they were,’’ Sánchez remarked. “They went into those communities and interacted in a very real and meaningful way. That's something I think that strategists or consultants don't always get. It's not just about pumping out lots of television commercials.”.

    Amid those successes for Latino Democrats, Florida, home to one of the largest Latino electorates in the country, was a different story. Republicans held all three majority-Latino districts in the Sunshine State, though former news anchor Eliott Rodriguez, the son of Cuban immigrants, came within half a percentage point of unseating GOP Rep. María Elvira Salazar in a district that backed Trump by 15 points in 2024.

    BOLD PAC did have a victory to celebrate in Florida, with Rep. Darren Soto, the deputy chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, narrowly prevailing in a district that Republicans redrew as one that no longer had a Latino majority.

    “The redistricting wars ended up failing because of the investment by BOLD PAC,’’ Soto mentioned.

    #6882. Industry News: Finnair Celebrates International Men’s Day With All-Male Crew On Flight

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (894 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Finnair Celebrates International Men’s Day With All-Male Crew On Flight

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (894 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that there’s still quite a gender gap in the airline industry, with a disproportionate number of pilots being male, and a disproportionate number of flight attendants being female.
    • Today is (apparently) International Men’s Day.
    • The crew consisted of 10 people, comprised of two pilots and eight flight attendants.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that there’s still quite a gender gap in the airline industry, with a disproportionate number of pilots being male, and a disproportionate number of flight attendants being female. Airlines will sometimes have special celebrations with all-female crews, so here’s an interesting twist on that.

    Today is (apparently) International Men’s Day. We often see airlines commemorate International Women’s Day, but there aren’t many airlines that celebrate the equivalent for men… well, except Finnair! The airline has today operated its annual flight with an all-male crew. This was the case for Finnair flight AY1331, from Helsinki (HEL) to London (LHR), using an Airbus A350-900.

    The crew consisted of 10 people, comprised of two pilots and eight flight attendants. The gate agents were also all men. So, why is this key? Finnair highlights how only around 10% of cabin crew at the airline are male, but the manufacturer hopes to see that number grow in the future.

    I think this is a fun concept, and it would be nice to see a closer to 50/50 gender ratio in both the cockpit and cabin, as it would show that everyone is given a fair chance at such a career.

    I think it’s worth acknowledging that at many airlines, hiring of flight attendants is still primarily or exclusively based on gender. Now, the policies do vary significantly by airline, but perhaps an extreme example is India’s largest airline, IndiGo, which only hires female flight attendants. It’s literally written on the application, that it’s a job for “Female Indian nationals.”.

    It’s all so strange, because the airline has this super enthusiastic page about the importance of diversity in the workplace, and says “all employment decisions are made solely on the basis of merit and qualifications, without regard to a candidate’s gender…” You mean except the single largest portion of your workforce, which is cabin crew?

    Tech Report: Standing Athwart Pumpkin Tyranny

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A pumpkin spice latte is on the menu at every coffee shop.
    • Through October and November, pumpkin is in everything everywhere all the time.
    • Abigail Anthony is a staff writer at National Review.

    A pumpkin spice latte is on the menu at every coffee shop. Sometimes, the drink is served in a pumpkin-shaped mug. To lure in customers for brunch, quaint cafes serving pumpkin pancakes put a chalkboard sign on the sidewalk saying, “COME IN FOR GOURD VIBRATIONS!” Each bakery has pumpkin scones, pumpkin pie, pumpkin banana bread, and pumpkin coffee cake. An attempt to order an old fashioned will be met with an invitation from the demoralized bartender, “Do you want to try our pumpkin spice old fashioned?” The pen at the bank is topped with a rubber pumpkin; this way, customers know that all the money is kept safe. Little plastic pumpkins are in the windows displays at clothing shops, or beside the cashiers (who work in front of pumpkin-flavored nicotine patches). Squashes are piled high in cardboard bins by the entrance of every grocery store. I reach for what I think is my favorite chai tea blend on the shelves — but alas! It is now pumpkin chai with an orange label.

    Through October and November, pumpkin is in everything everywhere all the time. Anything edible is infused, swirled, drizzled, and dusted with pumpkin. You cannot escape the flavor: pumpkin cereal, pumpkin protein powder, pumpkin bagels with pumpkin cream cheese. The Asian aisle has frozen Kung Pao-mpkin Dumplings. Dog treats are flavored like a pumpkin spice latte because everyone must participate, no exceptions. Longstanding favorites are replaced, so French fries are now pumpkin fries. That peculiar squash always sneaks its way into a dish, and so the stuffed raviolis have a little bit of pumpkin. Despite its omnipresence, the pumpkin surprises you: The waiter arrives at the table with a salad that is topped — just for this week — with toasted pumpkin seeds. (Of course, the utensils are wrapped in a flimsy brown napkin dotted with little orange pumpkins.) Even things we thought were reliably mint, like gum and the dentist’s fluoride, are pumpkin spice.

    Abigail Anthony is a staff writer at National Review.

    On “ Standing Athwart Pumpkin Tyranny”.

    Aer Lingus unveils premium economy, latest business class for its Airbus A330s

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (778 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Aer Lingus declared a major overhaul of its Airbus A330 fleet, modernizing the interior of the aging jets with a complete nose-to-tail retrofit.
    • Sources indicate that the Irish flag carrier will install its first-ever Premium Economy cabin, along with all-new lie-flat business class suites and updated economy seats.
    • Sources indicate that the retrofit will come to 10 of the airline's A330 jets, Aer Lingus noted in an announcement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Aer Lingus declared a major overhaul of its Airbus A330 fleet, modernizing the interior of the aging jets with a complete nose-to-tail retrofit.

    Sources indicate that the Irish flag carrier will install its first-ever Premium Economy cabin, along with all-new lie-flat business class suites and updated economy seats. The airline stated it will also continue to offer free Starlink Wi-Fi on the refurbished planes.

    Sources indicate that the retrofit will come to 10 of the airline's A330 jets, Aer Lingus noted in an announcement. The airline has a total of 10 A330-300 jets in service, along with two long-range A330-200s, according to Planespotters.net. It was not immediately clear what would happen to the two A330s that are not included in the retrofit.

    Review: Flying Aer Lingus business class across the Atlantic in its current A330 configuration.

    Aer Lingus described the project as one of its "most significant investments in the onboard customer experience in more than a decade.".

    "Our ambition here is simple," Aer Lingus CEO Lynn Embleton said in a statement. "We want to give our customers greater choice, comfort and connectivity, while creating an experience that feels unmistakably Aer Lingus.".

    The retrofitted jets will fly transatlantic routes to North America, the airline said, starting on Oct. 1 with flights EI104 and EI105 between Dublin Airport (DUB) and Fresh York's John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK).

    Let's take a closer look at the retrofit.

    Premium economy cabins have become much more widespread among airlines over the past decade, with carriers capitalizing on customers who are willing to pay a premium for more comfort, but are still price-sensitive and won't pay for business class.

    Aer Lingus is late to the trend, but clearly ready to commit. The airline will install four rows of premium economy seats in a 2-3-2 configuration for a total of 28 seats.

    The airline chose the Recaro R4 seat, which features a built-in leg-rest and a footrest at each seat, as well as privacy wings at the head to provide a bit of separation between seat-mates. The premium economy seats will have 38 inches of pitch and 8 inches of recline, as well as a width of 18-19 inches.

    Premium economy will also have its own cabin service, with a three-course meal and drinks throughout the flight, along with amenity kits, bedding, and "noise-reducing" headphones to use during the flight.

    The fresh cabin will be priced squarely in between coach and business class, with fares starting at €700 each way, or about $768.

    The business-class cabin will see a major upgrade, bringing a fresh latest product to replace one that has become dated.

    Recent findings suggest that the cabin will feature 28 business-class suites across seven rows in a 1-2-1 layout, giving every passenger direct aisle access. That's two fewer seats than on the current A330-300, but a major improvement since alternating rows in the existing cabin are configured in a sort of 1-2-2 layout.

    According to recent reports, the Collins Elevation suites feature closing privacy doors — a first for Aer Lingus. Each seat converts to a 78-inch long fully flat bed, and will offer wireless and USB-C charging options.

    It has been revealed that aer Lingus states that it also plans to revamp its onboard dining experience to showcase "seasonal Irish ingredients and contemporary culinary influences," although the airline did not share specifics. There will also be a self-service bar with drinks and snacks in the cabin.

    The economy cabin will also see new seats with a handful of features aimed at keeping passengers comfortable on long flights, including a six-way adjustable leather headrest.

    Recent findings suggest that every economy seat in the 2-4-2 cabin will have a 4K seat-back screen with Bluetooth connectivity for headphones, plus USB-C charging. A new in-flight snack station will have bites available after the main meal service.

    The design of economy and the entire plane is recognizably Aer Lingus, with a palette heavy on greens and whites with customized mood lighting to accent the on-board experience.

    Aer Lingus has offered a pleasant business-class product with stellar on-board service and decent availability, but there's no denying that its "hard product" has fallen behind the times. The newly introduced refresh will bring the airline up to snuff with competitors, and should elevate the overall product to match the service provided by the excellent cabin crew.

    The new premium economy cabin, meanwhile, offers travelers a new way to fly to Ireland and beyond with more space for a more comfortable journey, while helping Aer Lingus capture an increasingly key passenger segment.

    Overall, we're excited to see the new Aer Lingus hit the skies next fall!

    Recent findings suggest that ‘Fox News @ Night’ anchor Trace Gallagher reports on Democrat Mary Peltola defeating GOP nominee Dan Sullivan in the Alaska U.S. Senate race, flipping the ninth GOP-held seat.

    According to recent reports, rep. Nick Begich, R-Alaska, won re-election to Alaska’s lone House seat Wednesday, surviving a Democratic wave that flipped both the Senate seat and the governor’s mansion.

    Begich, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump, defeated independent challenger Bill Hill, a commercial fisherman and retired teacher backed by the Alaska Democratic Party, following the state’s ranked-choice voting tabulation.

    According to recent reports, begich’s victory, called at 9:27 p.m. ET on Wednesday – more than two weeks after Election Day – stood in sharp contrast to the rest of Alaska’s top-of-the-ticket results, where voters handed Democrats major breakthroughs despite Trump winning the state by 13% in 2024.

    HUNDREDS OF SUBPOENAS FLY IN DOJ’S ‘DECOY DAN’ PROBE AS DEMOCRAT PELTOLA DECLARED WINNER IN ALASKA.

    Industry observers note that rep. Nick Begich, R-Alaska, continues to show political strength in the state that has flipped Democratic in this midterm election cycle. (Nathaniel Wilder/Bloomberg via Getty Images).

    The race was among the final House contests called nationally after the Nov. 3 general election, offering a rare bright spot for Republicans in a midterm cycle that saw Democrats seize control of both chambers of Congress. Democrats thus far hold a 257-172 majority in the House, having flipped 46 seats to just three for Republicans. There are three races that remain too close to call.

    "This process requires engagement, and the perspectives brought forward during the campaign added value for Alaskans as they made key decisions about their vote in this race," Begich said in a statement after his victory.

    Hill, who campaigned on lowering costs, curbing massive money in politics and pushing back against billionaires, stated he called Begich to concede and congratulate him.

    "I wished him well as he continues representing Alaska in Congress, because all Alaskans have a stake in his success," Hill mentioned in a statement.

    ALASKA DEM PELTOLA DEFEATS SULLIVAN, FLIPPING 9TH GOP SENATE SEAT AFTER 'DECOY DAN' UPROAR.

    In a recent development, one day before Begich’s race was called, Democrat Mary Peltola unseated second-term Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska. Peltola — who previously represented Alaska in the U.S. House before losing to Begich in 2024 — became the first Alaska native elected to the Senate and the first Democrat to win a Senate race in the state in nearly two decades. Her victory cemented a 56-44 Democratic Senate majority, the party's largest since 2009.

    "As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my career to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans’ support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," Peltola wrote on X.

    Democrats also secured the Alaska governor’s office for the first time in nearly 30 years, with Democrat Jonathan S. Kreiss-Tomkins winning the open-seat race to succeed term-limited Republican Gov. Mike Dunleavy.

    Sources indicate that throughout the House campaign, Begich pitched himself as an effective advocate aligned with Trump’s push to expand oil, gas and resource development in Alaska. But the final stretch of the race was overshadowed by controversy surrounding Democrat Eric Hafner, a perennial candidate with no ties to Alaska who is presently serving a sentence in a federal prison in Upcoming York following a 2022 conviction for threatening to kill judges, police officers and others.

    PELTOLA SAYS ALASKA ‘VOTED FOR CHANGE’ IN SENATE RACE.

    In a recent development, hafner, whose state election booklet biography made no mention of his incarceration, captured nearly 8% of the first-round vote. In the closing weeks of the race, Hill’s campaign distributed stickers and yard signs branding Hafner a "fake ‘Democrat,’" while state party officials spent thousands of dollars on text messages to clarify that Hill was the party’s endorsed candidate after mysterious, unsourced texts circulated promoting Hafner.

    Hafner’s mother, Carol "Kitty" Hafner — who also lacks ties to Alaska and finished sixth in the state's August Senate primary — dismissed claims that her son was recruited as a spoiler, writing in an email to The Associated Press that his runs have been "entirely independent of any influencers" and adding, "Tell President Trump to Pardon Eric Hafner!".

    Controversy over alleged ballot spoilers also marked the Senate race, where independent candidate Dan J. Sullivan Jr. drew suspicion due to sharing a name with the Republican incumbent. Following reports that members of Peltola’s team helped recruit Sullivan Jr. into the race, the U.S. Justice Department opened a criminal investigation and Gov. Dunleavy ordered a state inquiry. Peltola has repeatedly denied any involvement.

    "I personally know that I am innocent, so I don’t spend a lot of time hand-wringing" about it, Peltola noted Wednesday.

    • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is signaling Democrats will move rapidly on immigration legislation when the party reclaims the House in January, while acknowledging it still has work to do in shaping its healthcare agenda.
    • Jeffries, who is expected to secure his spot as the next speaker during a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday, identified immigration and health care as among the top priorities for the incoming majority during a Tuesday news conference.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, house Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., holds a news conference in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is signaling Democrats will move rapidly on immigration legislation when the party reclaims the House in January, while acknowledging it still has work to do in shaping its healthcare agenda.

    Jeffries, who is expected to secure his spot as the next speaker during a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday, identified immigration and health care as among the top priorities for the incoming majority during a Tuesday news conference.

    Sources indicate that “One of the things that we need to do is to move the Dream and Promise Act for DACA recipients and TPS recipients,” Jeffries said, referring to a Democratic bill introduced last year. “We should actually move that bill immediately.”.

    The proposal aims to create a path to citizenship for certain Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals recipients and Temporary Protected Status holders. Similar legislation has been a top priority for Democrats in both chambers for more than a decade, with Democrats unable to advance this bill in the House while Republicans have held the majority.

    Jeffries also reiterated his calls to rein in Immigration and Customs Enforcement and redirect funding allocated to the agency through Republicans' budget law known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, while expressing a desire for bipartisan cooperation on immigration more broadly.

    “We think the border should be safe and strong and secure, and we think our immigration system overall is broken,” Jeffries stated. “We need to fix it in a comprehensive way, and certainly, it's our hope that a handful of Republicans will be willing to join us, so we can fix it in a bipartisan way.”.

    On healthcare, however, Jeffries offered fewer specifics, suggesting Democrats still have decisions to make before taking control of the chamber. Democrats broadly agree on the need to restore subsidies for plans purchased through health insurance markets that expired at the end of 2025. But the question of what additional steps the party should pursue with the goal of expanding coverage and lowering prices is likely to be a major test of Democratic leadership’s ability to find consensus among its robust fresh majority.

    When asked how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that's all part of an ongoing conversation.”.

    The Newly introduced York Democrat outlined several broader healthcare priorities, including reversing Medicaid cuts enacted under President Donald Trump, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits, all of which Democrats have vowed to do over the last year.

    “Out of the gate, what we clearly have to do is fix our broken healthcare system in terms of the damage that's been done by Donald Trump and MAGA extremists over the last two years, and that clearly involves reversing the Medicaid cuts and extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits, and beginning to engage in supporting medical research, particularly things like research for pediatric cancer,” Jeffries added.

    Democrats established a healthcare working group earlier this Congress, led by Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y. and Terri Sewell, D-Ala., to gather perspectives and develop policy proposals as the party works toward a broader agenda.

    Without an confirmed challenger, Jeffries has expressed confidence that he’ll secure the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who have said they remain “undecided” ahead of Wednesday’s elections. Jeffries, who was introduced as “Speaker Jeffries” on election night, said last week he was “very confident we’ll get there” and confirmed that the caucus will hold a recorded vote in the contest.

    Sources indicate that rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to go forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives, many aligned with the Democratic Socialists of America, had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

    Jeffries remarked Tuesday the approach mirrors the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who is best positioned to lead based on “track record, experience and vision.”.

    Industry News: World Of Hyatt Status Revamps For 2027—Award Stacking And Newly introduced Benefit Choices, But Cuts Come Also

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog.
    • Hyatt will finally let members combine a free night certificate with a confirmed suite upgrade starting January 1, 2027.
    • This isn’t an across the board improvement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

    Hyatt will finally let members combine a free night certificate with a confirmed suite upgrade starting January 1, 2027. I’ve wanted that for years. They’re also extending milestone free night certificates from 180 days to a year, and adding rewards after just 10 qualifying nights.

    This isn’t an across the board improvement. Suite upgrades will expire sooner. The suite upgrade choice at 50 nights gets cut in half. And My Hyatt Concierge becomes something you select alongside other rewards, rather than something everyone automatically receives at 60 nights. Free parking will no longer be an automatic benefit on award stays for Globalists.

    In a recent development, when I covered Hyatt’s last major status benefit refresh in November 2023, I liked it overall. They made awards transferable, added choices, and let members try Globalist benefits before earning Globalist. Guest of Honor became limited, but the Milestone Rewards themselves mostly got better.

    This time there are new and better options. I genuinely like a lot of the choices, but there are real tradeoffs. Hyatt is pitching the changes as more choice and flexibility, based on listening to members. That’s actually fair for much of this, though I don’t think members told them what they really wanted was for suite upgrade to expire up to a year earlier.

    Hyatt will allow members to combine eligible awards on the same reservation, including Suite Upgrade Awards, Guest of Honor Awards and the new Free Parking Awards. This fixes one of the problems I’ve been complaining about for years. A free night certificate is something you often want to use on a special leisure stay. That’s also when a suite may matter most, especially traveling with family. When I didn’t want to use a free night certificate was a work trip by myself. Free night awards had a lot less value to me because I had to give up a confirmed suite to use them. But being able to use the two awards together makes both more valuable. Combining Guest of Honor with a suite upgrade is useful, too. You can give someone Globalist treatment and confirm their suite ahead of time, rather than leaving the room upgrade to availability when they arrive. Hyatt also promises an enhanced Pay My Way experience, letting members mix awards, points, cash and Points + Cash by night. Online selection, gifting and redemption will be available for eligible awards. Pay My Way and stacking, by the way, really do all work together. Hyatt offers me this illustration, Let’s say a member is making a three night booking. Assuming both the Standard Suite was available for the duration, and there is award inventory available on the selected dates (just like today) – yes, a member could apply a Suite Upgrade Award to the whole stay, a Free Parking award to the whole stay, a Guest of Honor Award to the whole stay, and then pay for the reservation using points on one night, a promotional Free Night Award on another night, and cash on the third night.
